name: Kopere Dashboard
description: A modular administrative workspace for Moodle that unifies Kopere tools, permissions, KPIs, audit trails and institutional workflows behind one interface.
description_html:
Administrative workspaceKopere foundation

Kopere Dashboard

Give administrative teams one operational workspace instead of sending them through dozens of unrelated Moodle administration screens.

The dashboard provides the shared navigation, layout, permissions, indicators and audit layer used by internal modules and by several independent plugins in the Kopere family.

One workspace, different roles
  • Academic and registrar routines.
  • Course and user lookup.
  • Documents, contracts and requests.
  • Reporting and operational indicators.
  • Backup, diagnostics and administrative tools.
  • Separate permissions for modules and sensitive actions.
Modular architecture
Features can live as internal dashboard modules or independent local_kopere_* plugins while still appearing in the same navigation and permission model.
Role-oriented access
Registrar, finance, coordination, support and administrators can receive only the tools relevant to their work instead of inheriting broad access to the whole administration tree.
Audit trail
Important actions can record who performed them, when they happened, which module was involved and which record was affected.

A foundation for the Kopere ecosystem

The dashboard is useful on its own, but its larger role is architectural: it gives other Kopere plugins a consistent administrative shell, shared visual language and common permission surface so each new tool does not need to invent another back office.

name: Boost Magnific
description: Modern, highly configurable theme designed to transform the visual experience of courses.
description_html:
The Boost Magnific theme has just received a fantastic update: dark mode! -

With the new dark mode, you can navigate and study in a much more eye-friendly environment, especially in low-light conditions. The feature automatically adapts to your device settings or can be manually enabled through the top menu.

Today I present the modification in Moodle to allow teachers to customize icons. From now on, the teacher can create an activity and choose the icon they want to display on the viewing page. This way, the Moodle™ Software provides the student with a more engaging experience, presenting an icon that precisely reflects the content of the activity.

Transform the appearance of your Moodle with ease! Now, you can customize the homepage and footer using a modern and intuitive editor. Create unique blocks that reflect your identity and make your Moodle not only beautiful but also irresistible.

The Boost Magnific theme represents a revolution in Moodle design, providing a streamlined and clean environment that enhances the online learning experience. This innovative theme has been carefully developed to transform the Moodle interface, significantly improving usability and the aesthetics of the virtual learning environment.

One notable feature of Boost Magnific is the optimization of various blocks and sections, offering smoother and more intuitive navigation for users. Administrators will find configuration buttons strategically placed throughout the system, providing easy access to customization options. This approach makes it easy to tailor Moodle to the specific needs of each institution or instructor.

Furthermore, the menu has been enhanced to provide a more efficient navigation experience. Icons have been skillfully placed next to menus, contributing to a more attractive and functional layout. This thoughtful arrangement not only improves aesthetics but also optimizes accessibility, making it more intuitive for users to locate resources and tools.

With Boost Magnific, the clean and modern aesthetic is not just about appearance but rather a strategy to facilitate focus on educational content. This theme represents a significant leap in the evolution of Moodle, making the online learning process more enjoyable, efficient, and adaptable to the ever-changing needs of digital education.

Problems and bugs

name: Mod Super Video
description: Advanced video player with controls, integrations, and detailed reports.
description_html:
With the aim of providing a more dynamic and customizable teaching experience, I present the Super Video Module, a tool that enhances Moodle's capabilities by allowing easy addition of YouTube, Google Drive, or Vimeo videos.

A notable feature of Super Video is its adaptability to Moodle. The video player automatically adjusts its width to avoid inconveniences, ensuring that the content is displayed in an optimized manner-neither too small nor excessively large. Say goodbye to the small and ugly YouTube player...

Additionally, Super Video prioritizes the continuity of student progress. The system automatically saves the point where the student left off, providing a seamless and personalized learning experience. When the student returns to the video, the player automatically positions them at the exact point where they paused, eliminating the need to search manually.

An additional innovation is the visual map bar located below the video. This bar provides a visual representation of the actual percentage of the video that the student has watched. This approach prevents the student from skipping to the end of the video without consuming all the content, promoting more careful viewing and a deeper understanding of the material.

Support for Distraction-Free Design

We are excited to announce that Moodle Mod Supervideo now offers support for Distraction-Free Design, addressing a recent community request (see issue #34).

The Distraction-Free Design has been developed to provide a more focused and immersive viewing experience, allowing users to watch videos without additional distractions. With this new feature, the interface elements have been simplified and reorganized, creating a cleaner and more minimalist environment.

Integration with OttFlix

The Super Video plugin now offers full integration with OttFlix, a secure video hosting and streaming platform equipped with advanced protection technologies against copying and piracy.

If you don't yet have an OttFlix account and want to protect your video lessons with DRM, dynamic watermarking, and full compatibility with Moodle™ Software, get in touch to request access to the platform.

Once your account is created, you can start uploading your videos directly to OttFlix and use them securely in your courses, ensuring a safe and reliable experience for your students.

Kapture

Now, it's possible to record both microphone and system audio, offering a complete experience. With features such as countdown, camera reversal, and camera size configuration, Kapture makes the creation of video lessons and tutorials more flexible and adaptable to the teacher's needs.

Furthermore, uploading slides, documents, and spreadsheets while recording the video lesson facilitates the incorporation of additional material, enriching the teacher's experience.

Kapture offers an integrated and efficient approach to video lesson production, simplifying the process and enhancing the options available to teachers in the Moodle environment.

Reports

Additionally, the Super Video generates comprehensive reports, providing instructors with valuable insights into student views and view maps. This detailed analysis enables continuous adjustments to the content and pedagogical approach, ensuring effective delivery of the material.

Global Settings

For administrators, the global settings functionality offers comprehensive customization. It is possible to set default fields for all videos, ensuring consistency throughout the learning environment. However, flexibility is not compromised, as instructors have the freedom to modify these data for specific videos without affecting global settings.

To access these settings, simply navigate to the Site Administration section, select "Plugins," then "Activity Modules," and finally choose "Super Video." Here, customization options are at your fingertips, allowing refined adaptation to the specific needs of each course.

Problems and bugs with the Boost Magnific theme should be reported on the GitHub Issue Tracker: https://github.com/EduardoKrausME/moodle-mod_supervideo/issues.

Questions about the theme can be submitted on the Moodle Forum: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/view.php?id=2404.

name: Alternative File System
description: Move Moodle's filedir to AWS S3 or DigitalOcean Spaces and serve files through remote object storage for scalable, shared infrastructure.
description_html:
Object storageMoodle filedir

Alternative File System

Move moodledata/filedir away from one server disk and let Moodle read and serve files through remote object storage.

The plugin currently supports AWS S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces and is designed for environments where file growth, multiple application nodes or storage maintenance make a local-only filedir increasingly painful.

Supported storage
  • AWS S3.
  • DigitalOcean Spaces.
  • S3-compatible behavior may depend on the endpoint and should be validated before production use.
  • CDN delivery can be combined with the storage architecture when the selected provider and deployment support it.
Shared file storage
Object storage provides a common file location for clustered or multi-node Moodle deployments instead of binding filedir to one application server.
Controlled migration
Existing local filedir content can be transferred to the configured remote storage before the alternative file-system class becomes the active source.
tool_objectfs transition
A migration path can detect an existing tool_objectfs setup, reuse relevant settings and validate the new destination before switching the file-system class.

Why move filedir at all?

On larger sites, local filedir eventually becomes an infrastructure problem: disks grow, backups get heavier, horizontal scaling needs shared storage and server replacement becomes entangled with a large content volume.

Object storage does not magically make every request faster, but it separates application compute from file capacity and gives operations a storage layer that can scale, replicate and be managed independently.

Activation is explicit: after the remote destination is prepared, Moodle must be configured to use \local_alternative_file_system\external_file_system as its alternative file-system class in config.php.

name: Kopere APP Mobile
description: Mobile integration for Moodle with offline-aware content delivery, optimized file access and native app workflows.
description_html:
Mobile integrationOffline-aware

Kopere APP Mobile

Keep Moodle course content usable when connectivity is slow, intermittent or temporarily unavailable, without turning the LMS into a separate mobile backend.

The plugin exposes Moodle-side services and file delivery behavior used by the dedicated app, including offline-friendly handling for supported resources and repository files.

Designed for real connectivity constraints
  • Supported resources can be cached or downloaded for later access.
  • External repository files can be served instead of redirected when offline delivery is requested.
  • Course and progress data continue to use Moodle APIs and permissions.
  • No Moodle core modification is required.
Course content
Supports offline-aware delivery for common resources such as folders, pages, files, URLs, pictures and integrated modules.
File optimization
Lets the app request a file representation suitable for mobile and offline consumption instead of depending on a live redirect.
Moodle-native access
Authentication, permissions and course data remain in Moodle rather than being duplicated in a parallel platform.
Offline availability depends on the resource or activity involved. Content that requires live server state may still need an internet connection.

name: Copy and Paste Modules
description: Copy and paste activities and resources between courses with just a few clicks.
description_html:
Copy and Paste Modules

Copy one or more course activities and resources, move to another course or section, and paste them without rebuilding the content manually.

A persistent course clipboard

Teachers can copy an individual activity or use Moodle's bulk selection to place several items on the clipboard. The clipboard remains available while navigating to another course, so the destination does not need to be open at the same time as the source.

When pasting, the teacher chooses the destination section and the exact insertion position instead of being limited to a generic paste-at-the-end action.

Reuse the same selection more than once

A successful paste does not automatically clear the clipboard. The same copied activities can therefore be reused in multiple courses or sections without returning to the original course for every copy. A separate clear action is available when the clipboard is no longer needed.

Permission-aware copying

Copy, paste and clear operations are protected by the current Moodle session, and the plugin revalidates permissions for both the source and destination when content is pasted. The interface is shown only to users allowed to manage the copy workflow in the course.

Failures do not destroy the clipboard

If an item cannot be restored at the destination, the failure is reported for that activity while the clipboard remains available. This makes multi-item copying more practical because one failed item does not force the teacher to repeat the whole selection process.

name: Kopere BI
description: More than 100 Moodle reports and dashboards covering learning, access, courses, users, assessments, activities, enrolments and operational analytics.
description_html:
Business intelligence100+ reports

Kopere BI

Turn Moodle's operational data into dashboards people can use without starting every management question with a custom SQL query.

Kopere BI combines ready-to-use reports with charts, interactive tables, information cards, maps and custom Mustache presentations for administrators, coordinators, managers and educators.

Coverage across Moodle
  • Students, users and instructors.
  • Courses, content and enrolments.
  • Access, login and activity indicators.
  • Grades, assessments and completion.
  • Quiz, forum, SCORM, assignment and feedback activity.
  • Competencies, badges and learning plans.
  • Revenue and other institutional indicators where data is available.
Visual dashboards
Use ApexCharts, KPI cards and custom layouts to make trends and distributions visible without exporting everything first.
Operational tables
Large result sets can use searchable, sortable and paginated DataTables with export options according to the report implementation.
Custom presentation
Reports are not limited to one table format; Mustache output can present the same data as cards, summaries, lists or specialized management views.

Learning analytics without opening the event log on every page

The learning-analytics area includes operational dashboards such as overview indicators, learner attention queues, course health, Student 360, progress-versus-grade analysis and learning momentum.

These dashboards can read compact snapshot tables rebuilt by scheduled tasks instead of repeatedly aggregating the full standard log when a user opens a page, which is the difference between an analytics screen and a denial-of-service attack wearing a nice chart.

Kopere Dashboard foundation: the current plugin depends on local_kopere_dashboard, which provides the shared administrative workspace used by Kopere BI.

name: Star Rating
description: Collect quick star ratings and track student feedback.
description_html:
Star ratings inside Moodle courses

Allow learners to rate a course from 1 to 5 stars and show the average directly in the block. The block can also be placed alongside supported activity contexts such as Questionnaire.

Simple rating flow
One familiar five-star interaction with no separate survey workflow.
Visible average
The block exposes the aggregated course rating where learners can see it.
Course placement
Teachers or administrators can add the block where course feedback is most useful.

name: User Field DB
description: Create profile fields connected to information stored in the database.
description_html:
Database-backed user profile fields

Create profile fields whose options come from a Moodle database table, which is useful when values such as departments, branches or cost centers must stay consistent instead of becoming free-text variations.

Dynamic options
Update the source table and the available profile values follow the maintained data set.
Cleaner data
Controlled values reduce spelling variants and inconsistent organizational metadata.
Reporting-friendly
Structured profile values can be reused by reporting and segmentation workflows.

name: Moodle Course Backup
description: Automate Moodle course backups to FTP, restore archived courses and migrate backup sets between Moodle installations through a token-based transfer workflow.
description_html:
Course backupRestore and migration

Moodle Course Backup

Move course backups out of the day-to-day Moodle interface, organize them remotely and make restoration a controlled operational workflow instead of a hunt for old .mbz files.

The plugin automates course backups to FTP, organizes archives by course category and provides restoration tools for both stored backups and transfers from another Moodle installation.

Backup lifecycle
  1. Create the Moodle course backup.
  2. Transfer it to the configured FTP destination.
  3. Organize archives by course category.
  4. Browse stored backups from the restore interface.
  5. Queue restoration through Moodle tasks.
Remote archive
Keep course backup files on the configured FTP server instead of relying only on the Moodle application server's local disk.
Restore interface
Select backups from the stored archive and send restoration work to the normal Moodle processing flow.
Moodle-to-Moodle transfer
A new Moodle can connect to the previous installation using its wwwroot, an optional old server IP and a temporary transfer token, then list and queue selected remote backups.

Useful during server and platform migrations

The token-based transfer API means a migration does not have to begin by manually copying every backup file. The destination can discover the available remote backups, preserve source course/category context and queue the selected restores for CRON processing.

name: PDF Protect
description: Display PDFs through a controlled Moodle viewer that removes common download, print and text-copy paths to discourage casual redistribution.
description_html:
Controlled PDF viewingPDF.js viewer

PDF Protect

Publish a PDF as a Moodle activity when you want learners to read it in the browser without presenting the usual download, print and text-copy controls.

The activity uses a customized PDF.js-based viewer and Moodle file access instead of exposing the document through the browser's normal PDF interface.

Reduced casual extraction
  • Hides the standard download controls.
  • Suppresses the viewer's print controls.
  • Restricts normal text-selection/copy interaction.
  • Keeps the resource inside a Moodle activity context.
Custom viewer
Learners interact with the plugin's PDF.js presentation instead of the browser's native PDF toolbar.
Moodle file access
The document is served through Moodle's file handling and activity permissions rather than as an unrelated public file URL.
Simple authoring
Teachers add the PDF as a course activity and learners open it directly in the controlled viewer.
This is deterrence, not absolute DRM. Any document that can be rendered on a user's device can still be captured by determined users through screenshots, browser tooling or other methods. The plugin reduces common and accidental redistribution paths; it cannot make copying technically impossible.

name: SuperVideo Filter Player
description: Play video links using the modern SuperVideo player.
description_html:
Automatic Super Video rendering

Transform supported video links in Moodle content into the Super Video player automatically, keeping playback consistent without requiring authors to rebuild every embedded video manually.

  • Detects supported video links in filtered content.
  • Uses the Super Video presentation layer for a more consistent player experience.
  • Keeps video authoring simple while centralizing playback behavior.

name: OttFlix Repository
description: Browse and select OttFlix media from Moodle's repository picker instead of manually copying media references between systems.
description_html:
Moodle repositoryOttFlix library

OttFlix Repository

Bring the OttFlix library into Moodle's normal file-selection workflow so course authors can find media without leaving the editor to copy identifiers or URLs by hand.

Its job is selection and insertion. Playback remains the responsibility of the compatible Moodle media integration, keeping library browsing and rendering as separate concerns.

Author workflow
  1. Open Moodle's repository/file picker.
  2. Browse the available OttFlix media.
  3. Select the desired item.
  4. Insert its reference into the Moodle content being edited.
  5. Let the media layer render the compatible player.
No duplicate media catalog
OttFlix remains the media library; Moodle receives the selected reference through its repository workflow.
Editor-friendly
Teachers use the same repository picker they already know instead of switching applications every time they need a video.
Separation of responsibilities
The repository finds content; the media plugin handles how that content is embedded and played.

name: OttFlix Filter Player
description: Recognize OttFlix media references in Moodle content and render them with the OttFlix playback integration automatically.
description_html:
Media playerAutomatic embed

OttFlix Filter Player

Turn compatible OttFlix media references in Moodle content into the appropriate embedded player instead of leaving learners with a raw link.

This plugin is the rendering half of the integration: course authors can insert OttFlix content in Moodle, while the media layer recognizes that content and produces the player at display time.

Where it fits
  • OttFlix stores and manages the media.
  • The repository plugin helps authors select it.
  • The media plugin converts the reference into playback.
  • Moodle content keeps the normal editor and display workflow.
Automatic rendering
Compatible references are transformed when Moodle renders the content, reducing manual embed-code handling.
Reusable across content
The media layer can be used wherever Moodle's normal content rendering supports the configured media player.
Library stays external
The integration renders OttFlix media without turning Moodle into a second copy of the OttFlix library.

name: Helpdesk and Knowledge Base
description: Integrated ticketing and knowledge base with category teams, scheduled workflows, Kopere BI reporting and AI Bridge-assisted drafting.
description_html:
Service deskKnowledge base

Kopere Helpdesk

Bring support requests into Moodle so the ticket, user, course context, conversation and operational history stay in the same environment.

Users can open and follow tickets while support teams organize work by category, status and priority, add attachments, search conversations and keep reusable answers in the built-in knowledge base.

Operational workflow
  • Category-based support teams and routing.
  • Email notifications for new tickets and replies.
  • Ticket history for status, priority and category changes.
  • Scheduled reminders for unanswered requests.
  • Automatic closing of resolved tickets after the workflow period.
Kopere Dashboard
local_kopere_dashboard provides the administrative foundation used by the plugin.
Kopere BI
local_kopere_bi provides the reporting layer for ticket demand, categories, service time and support activity.
AI Bridge
local_ai_bridge centralizes AI routing used to assist with reply and knowledge-base drafting while keeping human review in the workflow.

Built for support teams, not only ticket storage

The Helpdesk combines ticket management, knowledge reuse, reporting and scheduled follow-up so pending work can be identified and acted on instead of disappearing into email threads or external systems.

name: EadFlix

  • Virtual keyboard for navigation
  • Highlighting of links and headings

  • Customizable color schemes

Frontpage

  • Three types of banners
  • Pricing list
  • Four resource lists
  • Four highlights lists
  • Customizable FAQs

Course Page

EadFlix features a modern course page with an optional info banner that can be enabled via settings.

Activity block system: when you upload an image, the activity is converted into blocks. This works with both Topics and Weekly formats.

Thanks and Sponsorship

name: Panda Video
description: Add Panda Video as a native Moodle activity with provider playback, secure URL/token handling and activity completion support.
description_html:
Video activityPanda Video

Panda Video

Use Panda Video as an actual Moodle activity instead of treating every course video as a generic external embed.

Teachers add a Panda-hosted video to the course structure, while the plugin handles provider playback, API-key integration, secure URL/token patterns and Moodle activity behavior.

Native course behavior
  • Dedicated Panda Video activity type.
  • Panda Video player inside the course.
  • Secure URL/token support.
  • Activity completion compatibility.
  • Activity summary and display settings.
Course structure
The video appears as a normal Moodle activity, so teachers can position and manage it alongside the rest of the learning sequence.
Provider integration
The site API key is configured once in the activity plugin and reused by the Panda integration instead of requiring authors to build embed code manually.
Part of a plugin family
Use repository_pandavideo for library selection and media_pandavideo when the goal is automatic embedding inside Moodle text content.

name: Panda Video Filter Player
description: Turn Panda Video links into players embedded in content.
description_html:
This plugin allows you to quickly insert videos hosted on Panda Video into any Moodle content area (labels, pages, books, forums, etc.) using the Moodle editor’s media icon.

Features

  • Automatically transforms Panda Video links into embedded players.
  • Easy to use: just paste the Panda Video link and you're done!
  • Works with the standard Moodle text editor media button.
  • Can be used in labels, pages, books, forum posts, quizzes, and more.

How to activate

To activate the plugin, go to: Site administration ' Plugins ' Filters ' Multimedia plugins ' Manage media players and enable the Panda Video Filter Player.

How to use

  1. Copy the Panda Video link in the following format: https://dashboard.pandavideo.com.br/#/videos/VIDEO_ID
  2. Paste the link into any Moodle text editor using the media button or directly into the content.
  3. The plugin will automatically detect and embed the video player.

name: Panda Video Repository
description: Browse the Panda Video library from Moodle's repository picker and insert selected videos into Moodle content without copying URLs manually.
description_html:
Moodle repositoryPanda Video library

Panda Video Repository

Browse your Panda Video account from Moodle's repository picker and insert a selected video directly where you are authoring content.

The repository removes the copy-URL-switch-window-paste cycle: authors select a library item through Moodle, and the media integration takes care of displaying the player.

Panda integration flow
  1. Configure the Panda API key in mod_pandavideo.
  2. Enable the Panda Video repository.
  3. Browse the Panda library from Moodle's picker.
  4. Select a video.
  5. Let media_pandavideo render the compatible player in content.
Library selection
Search and choose Panda-hosted content where Moodle authors already expect external repositories to appear.
No manual embed code
The selected reference can move through the normal editor workflow rather than asking every teacher to understand provider embed markup.
Shared credentials
The repository uses the Panda integration configured through mod_pandavideo instead of maintaining a second independent API-key setup.

name: Ead Training
description: Clean, accessible academic theme packed with customization options.
description_html:
At Ead Training, we believe in free education that is accessible to everyone, visually appealing in both content and design.

Accessibility Features

  • Integration with VLibras for automatic translation into Brazilian Sign Language (only for Brazilian Portuguese)
  • Text resizing and contrast options
  • Adjustable letter and line spacing
  • Virtual keyboard for navigation
  • Highlighting of links and headings
  • Text-to-speech content reading (when available in the browser)
  • Customizable color schemes

Frontpage

Ead Training offers two homepage options: the default Moodle layout and a customized version with editable blocks featuring the following elements:

  • Four Netflix-style slideshows
  • Three types of banners
  • Price list
  • Four resource lists
  • Four lists of key differentiators
  • Customizable FAQs

Course Page

Ead Training features a modern course page with an optional information banner, enabled via settings.

Activity block system: when an image is uploaded, the activity is transformed into a block. This works for both Topics and Weekly formats.

Changes to Moodle Structure

  • There have been many changes to the structure and order of items, especially on the Course Category page.
  • Selected courses now appear above the categories instead of below.
  • Buttons are now displayed inline rather than stacked vertically.

"My Courses" Page:

  • The order has been adjusted so the search field is now at the end of the list.
  • The search field starts small and expands when focused, saving space when not in use.

Modern Popup Profile

Popup-style display with a customizable top section and fully customizable background. Includes quick-access menus for:

  • View and edit profile
  • Grades
  • Calendar
  • Reports
  • Preferences
  • Switch profiles
  • Log out

Footer Block

The footer supports 0 to 4 fully customizable blocks. Use your creativity to design any content you want, with no limitations from rigid link or icon settings.

Even better: the "Made by" text can be removed directly in the settings at no additional cost.

Acknowledgments and Sponsorship

Special thanks to Diego from EadSuporte for the essential partnership and support.

name: System Status
description: Monitor services, availability, and technical indicators in real time.
description_html:
Public Moodle status page

Monitor site availability, current uptime, consecutive days online and outage history, then expose a read-only public page that can be shared with users or operational teams.

Cron frequency matters: the Moodle cron must run at least as often as the selected check interval or expected checks will be skipped.

Operational signals
  • Availability checks.
  • Continuous uptime.
  • Consecutive-day streak.
  • Outage history.
  • Public read-only view.

name: Slow Queries
description: Turn existing Moodle query logs into an admin interface for finding slow SQL, recurring bottlenecks, callers and CRON-versus-WEB performance problems.
description_html:
Database performanceAdmin-only

Slow Queries

Turn a table full of query timings into something an administrator can actually use to answer: which SQL is slow, how often does it happen, and where is it coming from?

The plugin reads an existing {log_queries} data source and provides filtering, triage and context for Moodle database performance investigations.

From symptom to caller
  • Filter by execution time and query metadata.
  • Separate CRON-originated queries from web requests.
  • Derive a practical caller from the captured backtrace.
  • Inspect SQL, parameters, errors and timing together.
  • Look for recurrence instead of chasing one isolated spike.
Performance triage
Start with the worst execution times, then narrow the problem by caller, request type and recurrence before touching indexes or application code.
Backtrace context
The UI skips the generic Moodle DML frames and surfaces the next meaningful frame, which is usually much closer to the component that triggered the database call.
Best-effort SQL reconstruction
Common parameter formats are parsed so positional values can be shown with the statement for investigation, while making no claim that every logger format can be reconstructed perfectly.
This is a viewer, not a query collector. The environment must already record query data in {log_queries}. Access is intentionally restricted because SQL, parameters and backtraces may contain sensitive operational information.

name: Kopere Email
description: Email messaging channel with additional communication features.
description_html:
Message outputBranded email

Kopere Email

Apply a consistent branded wrapper to Moodle notifications and create provider-specific subjects and HTML templates without patching every plugin that sends a message.

Centralized delivery layer
Moodle keeps generating notifications normally; Kopere Email controls the final email presentation and can migrate provider delivery away from the default email processor to avoid duplicates.
Global wrapper
Standardize branding, spacing and common links across notifications.
Per-provider templates
Override subject and HTML for the notification types where generic Moodle email is not enough.
Digest workflows
Reduce repetitive email traffic for supported grouped-conversation scenarios.

name: Child Course
description: Organize related courses and present access to child courses as an activity.
description_html:
Use one course as a controlled gateway to another

Child Course adds an activity in the parent course that can enrol the learner into a target course, map groups and synchronize completion or grades incrementally before redirecting the learner.

Stateful integration
Dedicated mapping and state tables keep enrolment and synchronization predictable instead of recalculating the entire relationship on every access.
Automatic enrolment
Optionally grant access when the learner opens the activity.
Group mapping
Use a fixed group or inherit relevant groups from the parent course.
Incremental synchronization
Scheduled and manual sync update changed completion and grade state without a full rebuild.

name: Scientific Calculator
description: Scientific calculator available as an activity within courses.
description_html:
Scientific Calculator inside the course

Give students a fast client-side scientific calculator for math, physics, engineering, finance and other STEM workflows without sending them to an external website.

Controlled expression parser
Expressions are tokenized, converted with the shunting-yard algorithm and evaluated from a defined operator/function set rather than passed to JavaScript eval().
Scientific functions
Trigonometry, logarithms, roots, powers, factorial, constants and common numeric helpers.
Local history
Recent results can be reused quickly during problem-solving.
No per-key server roundtrip
The calculator runs in the browser, keeping interaction immediate and server load minimal.

name: Public Sitemap
description: Generate a standards-compliant XML sitemap from public Moodle content while respecting visibility and guest-access rules.
description_html:
Public discoveryXML sitemap

Public Sitemap

Expose Moodle's public content through a valid XML sitemap so crawlers can discover the pages that are actually intended to be public.

The sitemap is generated from Moodle data instead of a manually maintained URL list, and the plugin respects visibility when deciding what can be exposed.

Public content sources
  • Site front page.
  • Visible course categories.
  • Visible courses eligible for public discovery.
  • Public Moodle blog entries.
  • Forums available in public or guest-accessible contexts.
  • Visible activities placed on the front page.
Dynamic XML
Generates absolute URLs and ISO-8601 modification dates using Moodle data at request time.
Automatic discovery hint
Adds a sitemap reference to the page head so compatible crawlers and SEO tools can detect the endpoint.
Visibility first
Hidden categories, hidden activities and content that should not be public are not treated as indexable pages.
A sitemap improves discovery, not ranking. The plugin helps search engines find public Moodle URLs; it does not promise higher search positions.

name: Kopere WP Bridge
description: Synchronize completed WooCommerce orders with Moodle course enrolments and cohorts using mapped products, signed webhooks and scheduled reconciliation.
description_html:
WooCommerceMoodle enrolment

Kopere WP Bridge

Turn WooCommerce purchases into Moodle access without maintaining a second enrolment workflow by hand.

Products can be mapped to courses and cohorts; when an order completes, the bridge identifies the customer, creates the Moodle account when necessary and applies the mapped access.

Order-to-access flow
  1. Map a WooCommerce product to one or more Moodle destinations.
  2. Receive the completed-order webhook.
  3. Validate the local token and WooCommerce HMAC signature.
  4. Resolve or create the Moodle user.
  5. Enrol in mapped courses and add to mapped cohorts.
  6. Record processing so reconciliation can safely retry pending items.
Product mappings
One commercial product can drive course enrolment, cohort membership or both, keeping catalog logic outside Moodle course administration.
Webhook validation
Incoming order events are checked using a local endpoint token and WooCommerce signature validation before access is processed.
Scheduled reconciliation
A scheduled task revisits recent completed sales so transient webhook failures do not silently become missing enrolments.

Designed for idempotent commerce workflows

The bridge treats the webhook as the fast path and scheduled synchronization as the safety net, which is much more reliable than assuming every external callback will arrive exactly once and at the perfect moment.

name: Kopere Proctoring
description: Policy-based quiz proctoring with explicit student rules, incident evidence, verifiable agreements, focus/fullscreen controls and attempt review.
description_html:
Exam integrityPolicy-based

Kopere Proctoring

Apply the controls an exam actually needs, explain them to the student before the attempt and preserve reviewable evidence when something happens during the assessment.

The plugin is built around independent policies rather than one opaque “proctoring mode”, so institutions can combine controls according to the assessment context.

Current policy families
  • Contract and honesty agreement.
  • Copy, cut, paste, print and context-menu restrictions.
  • Focus and tab/application change monitoring.
  • Fullscreen enforcement.
  • Notifications for relevant exam events.
  • Browser and environment security signals.
Student-visible rules
Mandatory conditions are presented before the exam starts, so monitoring is part of the declared assessment rules rather than hidden behavior.
Incident evidence
Attempt context and policy incidents can be reviewed later with timestamps and relevant environment information instead of relying on a single yes/no flag.
Extensible policies
Policies follow a shared discovery and lifecycle architecture, which keeps individual controls isolated and makes new evidence types possible without rewriting the entire proctoring flow.

Agreement with verifiable evidence

When the contract policy is enabled, the institution can present an honor code, privacy notice or exam rules before access is released. Acceptance can produce a PDF receipt with verification data, creating an auditable record that the learner received and accepted the declared conditions.

Different exams can use different controls

A low-stakes activity may need only an agreement, while a controlled final exam can combine fullscreen, focus, copy restrictions, security signals, notifications and teacher-controlled access. The goal is proportional control, not forcing every quiz into the same restrictive experience.

Signals are evidence, not a verdict. A focus change, fullscreen exit or browser anomaly can have legitimate causes. Kopere Proctoring records context for review and does not treat one incident as automatic proof of misconduct.

name: Video Progress
description: Track the video segments students actually watch, with completion, grades, timelines, analytics and synchronized learning interactions.
description_html:
Track what was actually watched

Video Progress turns video into a complete Moodle activity with progress based on the segments the learner really watched. Moving the playhead to the end does not produce 100% completion: skipped regions remain unwatched, while repeated regions increase playback time without artificially increasing the unique-content percentage.

The activity integrates completion, grades, reports and timelines so teachers can distinguish the last watched position, unique content watched, total playback time, repeated segments and audience drop-off points.

Video sources and learning resources

Video sources are extensible through subplugins and currently include uploads, direct URLs, YouTube and Vimeo. Activities can also include captions, Bloom-based learning objectives, support materials and synchronized content displayed at specific moments in the video.

  • Segment-based viewing progress and playback resume.
  • Completion rules based on a minimum percentage actually watched.
  • Gradebook integration using the watched percentage.
  • Individual and aggregated class timelines.
  • Most-watched, least-watched and audience drop-off analysis.
  • Optional forward-seeking restrictions and playback-speed limits.
  • WebVTT and SRT captions.
  • Bloom learning objectives and complementary materials.
  • Synchronized notes and mandatory quiz interactions during playback.
  • CSV export, progress reset, backup and restore, Privacy API and Moodle app integration.

Extensible architecture

Sources, objectives, materials and synchronized content are implemented through dedicated subplugin types, allowing new formats and video platforms to be added without changing the activity core.

name: Recertification
description: Run auditable recertification cycles that archive selected learner history before resetting progress, with simulation, scheduling and rollback-safe execution.
description_html:
RecertificationAudit-first reset

Kopere Recertification

Repeat a certification cycle without pretending the learner's previous cycle never existed.

Before selected progress is reset, the engine builds an execution plan, preserves configured history and files, validates the preservation phase and only then performs cleanup.

Archive first, reset second
  1. Build the plan in real course order.
  2. Create enabled history snapshots.
  3. Validate and copy enabled file archives through Moodle File API.
  4. Clean selected activity and system data only after preservation succeeds.
  5. Commit the cycle, then emit business events and notifications.
Transactional safety
Each user/course execution uses a Moodle lock and delegated transaction so a preservation or cleanup failure does not accept a partially reset cycle.
Real simulation
Simulation runs the same providers and selection logic inside a transaction that is always rolled back, including file-source validation without permanent file-pool side effects.
Auditable cycles
History, copied files, logs and notification records remain tied to the recertification cycle so the previous state can be reviewed later.

Scheduling that reflects certification reality

Course policies can reference enrolment, fixed annual dates, course completion, a certificate/reference provider or the last completed recertification cycle. Automatic cycles are queued per user, while administrative and bulk workflows remain independent so one failure does not poison an entire batch.

Before the due date
Scheduled state supports warning notifications without prematurely declaring the current certification invalid.
At the due date
The cycle becomes pending and is processed through an independent ad-hoc task for the learner.

Extensible data providers

Specialized recerttask_* providers isolate component-specific history and cleanup rules. The current package includes providers for quiz, forum, grades, activity completion, course completion, competency and enrolment, plus integrations such as Certificate Beautiful, Child Course, Super Video and Video Progress.

Generic cleanup is deliberately conservative: it is limited to eligible activity tables and approved user-bound conditions rather than guessing which records are safe to delete.

Recertification is not a blind reset button. The design intentionally makes preservation, validation, simulation and auditability part of the operation before destructive processing is accepted.

name: H5Prime Viewer
description: Use H5Prime as Moodle's H5P rendering layer while keeping content, metadata and saved state in Moodle's native H5P subsystem.
description_html:
H5P runtimeH5Prime

H5Prime Viewer

Replace the H5P presentation layer without inventing another activity, another content format or another content repository.

h5plib_vh5prime plugs into Moodle's H5P library-handler architecture and renders existing H5P content through the H5Prime runtime.

What stays in Moodle
  • H5P content and metadata.
  • Language and user context.
  • Saved user state supplied by Moodle.
  • Existing H5P workflows and content management.
Native handler integration
Registers H5Prime where Moodle expects an H5P library handler instead of patching core rendering code.
Bundled runtime assets
Ships the JavaScript, styles, templates and translations needed by the H5Prime viewer as part of the Moodle plugin.
No external account
Rendering does not depend on creating a separate hosted-service account just to display the H5P content already stored in Moodle.

A viewer, not a parallel H5P platform

The distinction matters: teachers continue creating and managing H5P through Moodle, while H5Prime is responsible for how compatible content is presented at runtime. That keeps ownership and lifecycle in Moodle and makes the rendering layer replaceable.

name: Missing Students
description: Identify inactive learners by course and review retention indicators, risk distribution, absence ranges and CSV exports.
description_html:
Missing Students

Identify learners who have been inactive for a meaningful period and turn course-access data into a practical retention dashboard.

Focus on learners who should actually be monitored

Missing Students works at course level and uses Moodle's completion-report population rules so the report focuses on participants who are relevant to course monitoring instead of treating every enrolled account as an equal retention case.

The inactivity threshold is configurable. The report distinguishes time since the learner last accessed the current course from the learner's last access to Moodle as a whole, giving teachers a clearer picture of whether the problem is course-specific or broader.

Retention dashboard

  • Course-access inactivity based on the learner's latest access to the current course.
  • Site-access inactivity based on the learner's latest Moodle access.
  • Indicators and risk distribution for quickly identifying the most urgent cases.
  • Absence ranges and a criticality ranking to support follow-up prioritization.
  • Filters that help teachers narrow the report to the learners who need attention.
  • CSV export for contact workflows, external analysis or institutional retention processes.

From data to follow-up

The plugin is intended to make inactivity actionable. Instead of presenting raw access logs, it organizes the information into a course-oriented view that can support outreach, tutoring, retention campaigns and other learner-support routines.

name: Private Notes
description: Give each learner a private per-user note area inside a course activity without exposing notes to other users.
description_html:
Private Notes

Give every learner a private writing space inside a Moodle course without exposing note content to classmates or teachers.

A private note attached to the learning context

Teachers can place a Private Notes activity next to a video, page, lesson or any other course content. Each learner opens the activity and writes with Moodle's standard editor, creating one personal note area for that activity.

The note belongs to the current authenticated user. The content API does not accept an arbitrary user id, so a learner cannot request another learner's note by changing a URL or request parameter.

Privacy by design

  • One private note per learner and activity.
  • Other learners never see the note.
  • Teachers do not receive a capability that exposes note text.
  • Optional teacher metadata can be disabled, aggregated only, or limited to learner identity and created/modified dates.
  • Individual teacher metadata deliberately excludes the note content itself.
  • No external service or client-side dependency is required.

Useful alongside course content

Private Notes is suitable for personal reflections, study reminders, observations while watching a lesson, preparation notes and other learner-owned writing that should stay inside Moodle without becoming a submission or discussion.

name: Branching Video
description: Create interactive branching videos with decisions, alternate paths, multiple endings, resume and learner path tracking.
description_html:
Branching Video

Create interactive videos in which learner decisions change what happens next, allowing alternate paths, reconnection points and multiple endings.

Decisions inside the video

Teachers add one or more videos and place decisions at specific timecodes. Each answer option can send the learner to another point in the same video, to another video, to another decision or directly to a named ending.

Paths do not need to remain permanently separate. Different branches can reconnect later, making it possible to model realistic scenarios without duplicating every scene.

Learning path tracking

  • Uploaded video, direct media URL, YouTube and Vimeo sources.
  • Decision history recorded for each learner.
  • Resume support for unfinished branching paths.
  • Teacher control over whether earlier choices may be changed.
  • Optional display of the completed path after the learner reaches an ending.
  • Completion can be tied to reaching a valid ending.

Reports for scenario analysis

Teacher reports show decision histories, option distribution, commonly used paths, abandonment points and reached endings. This makes the activity useful for simulations, case-based learning, consequence-driven training and other situations where the route taken is as important as the final destination.

name: GeniAI Chat
description: Add a course activity that exposes the GeniAI chat experience inside Moodle.
description_html:
GeniAI Chat

Place the GeniAI conversational experience directly inside a Moodle course as a standard course activity.

Course-level access to GeniAI

GeniAI Chat acts as the course activity layer for the local GeniAI service. Learners open the activity from the course and receive the configured GeniAI chat interface without leaving Moodle.

The activity passes the current course context to the GeniAI chat experience, allowing the conversation entry point to be presented as part of the normal course flow rather than as a separate site-wide tool.

Uses the shared GeniAI configuration

  • Uses the GeniAI name and operating mode configured by the local GeniAI plugin.
  • Shows the course-aware introductory messaging supplied by GeniAI.
  • Respects Moodle course login and the activity view capability.
  • Exposes management controls only to users who hold the GeniAI management capability.
  • Uses Moodle's standard activity-view event and completion-by-view behavior.
  • The activity module itself does not declare plugin-specific personal-data storage.

A simple activity wrapper

The module intentionally keeps its own settings small: the course activity provides the name, description and normal Moodle activity settings, while the conversational behavior is supplied by the installed local GeniAI plugin. This avoids duplicating provider and chat configuration inside every course activity.

name: Phrase Wall
description: Collect one short phrase from each learner and display the responses in a visual wall, optionally anonymously.
description_html:
Phrase Wall

Collect one concise contribution from each learner and display the class responses as a visual wall.

Short responses instead of long discussions

Phrase Wall is designed for reflections, summaries, takeaways, opinions, exit prompts and other activities where the teacher wants one focused sentence from each participant instead of a forum thread or long-form submission.

The teacher defines the maximum sentence length and whether learner names should be visible to participants. Each learner submits one phrase and the wall presents the class responses according to those settings.

Main features

  • One sentence per learner.
  • Configurable sentence limit from 60 to 280 characters.
  • Identified or anonymous participant-facing wall.
  • Optional editing of the learner's own sentence.
  • Teacher report that retains authorship even when the wall is anonymous.
  • Teacher ability to delete submissions.
  • Optional activity completion after submission.
  • Responsive interface for desktop and mobile use.

Simple learner and teacher workflows

Learners open the activity, write within the configured limit and submit. Teachers get a compact overview of participation without turning the activity into a conversation stream, while still retaining the management information required for moderation and follow-up.

name: AJAX Chat
description: Provide real-time course chat with text, recorded audio, attachments, reactions, polls and lightweight file-backed polling.
description_html:
AJAX Chat

Provide a live course chat with text, recorded audio, attachments, reactions and teacher-managed polls while keeping frequent read polling away from normal database-heavy page requests.

Real-time conversation inside the course

Learners can exchange text messages, record audio in supported browsers and attach files when those options are enabled. Users can react to messages and may edit or delete their own message during the first 60 seconds after sending it.

Teacher controls for live sessions

  • Enable or disable the chat when the conversation should be opened or paused.
  • Delete messages when moderation is required.
  • Block and unblock participants.
  • Create polls that remain pinned at the top or in a side panel until they are closed.
  • Set an availability date before which learners cannot read the history or use the composer.

Lightweight polling architecture

The chat maintains its frequently read state in files under the protected Moodle data area, including recent-message indexes and a lightweight event stream. This allows history and polling requests to read the chat state without repeatedly performing normal plugin SELECT queries on every browser poll.

Protected attachment delivery

Stored attachments remain outside the public web root and are served through opaque file identifiers. Active-content file types such as HTML, JavaScript and SVG are rejected, while non-media files are delivered as downloads.

name: Class Check-in
description: Register class attendance inside a configurable time window with optional code, IP and geolocation restrictions.
description_html:
Class Check-in

Register attendance during a controlled time window with optional code, network and geolocation checks.

A direct attendance workflow

The learner opens the activity during the configured window and uses the check-in action to register presence. Teachers can keep the process simple or add additional checks when the class context requires them.

A numeric code can be required and regenerated by the teacher. The activity can also compare the learner's detected public IP address with the reference IP captured by the teacher, or verify that the learner is within a configured geographic radius of a teacher-captured location.

Attendance controls and reporting

  • Configurable opening and closing window.
  • Optional 4- or 6-digit attendance code.
  • Optional same-public-IP validation against the teacher reference.
  • Optional browser geolocation validation within a configurable radius.
  • Report showing present and pending/absent learners.
  • Registration time, IP and location information when those checks are enabled.
  • Activity completion after a successful check-in.

Designed with realistic presence signals

IP matching is useful when the class shares the same network and public NAT address, but it is treated as a network signal rather than cryptographic proof of physical presence. Geolocation similarly depends on the position and accuracy reported by the learner's browser.

name: Link Collection
description: Organize external references into sections and enrich links with fetched titles, descriptions and cached thumbnails.
description_html:
Link Collection

Organize multiple external references into a structured Moodle activity with sections, metadata and cached thumbnails.

Build curated collections

Teachers create ordered sections such as weekly material, references or further reading and add multiple external links to each section. This keeps related resources together instead of filling the course page with separate URL activities.

When a link is saved, the plugin can retrieve useful page metadata and present the student view as a compact list of enriched references.

Main features

  • Multiple ordered sections inside one activity.
  • Multiple ordered links inside each section.
  • Metadata extraction from page title, description, Open Graph and Twitter Card tags.
  • Cached thumbnails stored through Moodle's file system.
  • Manual title and description overrides.
  • One-click metadata refresh for teachers.
  • Moodle cURL security checks for page and image URLs.
  • Activity completion by view.

Cleaner course organization

Link Collection is useful for reading lists, research references, weekly resources, curated websites and any course area where a teacher wants to maintain a group of external materials as one coherent activity.

name: Video Compare
description: Compare two or more videos side by side, answer comparison questions and create timestamp-to-timestamp comparisons.
description_html:
Video Compare

Put two or more videos into one activity so learners can compare content, answer questions and connect precise moments across sources.

Comparison as the learning task

Teachers add multiple videos and create required comparison questions. Questions can also be anchored to moments in two videos, helping learners compare specific evidence rather than relying only on a general impression.

Learners can watch videos side by side when screen space allows, switch between sources quickly and create timestamp-to-timestamp comparisons.

Independent tracking for every video

  • Uploaded videos, direct video URLs, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Separate watched-segment tracking for each video.
  • Resume from the learner's latest position.
  • Overall activity progress calculated from the individual video progress values.
  • Required comparison questions.
  • Timestamp comparisons linking evidence from different videos.

Teacher reporting

Reports combine per-video viewing progress, overall progress, completion of required questions, learner answers and timestamp comparisons. This makes the activity useful for comparing demonstrations, cases, techniques, perspectives or before/after examples.

name: Exit Ticket
description: Collect a short end-of-class formative reflection and review participation and responses in a teacher report.
description_html:
Exit Ticket

Collect a short private reflection at the end of a class and give teachers a fast overview of participation and understanding.

Two or three focused questions

Teachers configure a small set of open questions for the end of a lesson or class meeting. Each learner submits one private response containing their answers, keeping the activity deliberately lightweight.

When enabled, the learner can continue editing the response until the configured closing time.

A class-oriented report

  • Submission totals for the activity.
  • List of learners who have not yet responded.
  • Response rate for quick participation monitoring.
  • Answers grouped by question for easier review.
  • One activity instance can represent one specific class or lesson.

Useful for formative feedback

Exit Ticket supports quick end-of-class checks such as the most important idea learned, what remains unclear, or what should be revisited next. Because each instance represents one meeting, the course activity index can also serve as a simple history of class-by-class reflections.

name: Kopere Trail
description: Organize Moodle courses and other resources into larger learning trails without replacing Moodle's native completion and grading.
description_html:
Kopere Trail

Organize Moodle courses and external learning resources into larger learning journeys without replacing Moodle's native courses, activities, completion or grades.

A learning layer above individual courses

Kopere Trail gives learners a single journey that can span several Moodle courses and other resource types. The trail becomes the entry point, while the actual learning objects continue to live in their native systems.

Courses keep their own activities, completion rules, grades and competencies. The trail simply arranges those elements into stages and presents progress across the larger journey.

Extensible trail items

Trail stages can point to Moodle courses, URLs, HTML content, H5P and other item types provided through the plugin's subplugin architecture. This makes the trail model extensible without forcing every type of content into the core local plugin.

Enrollment and progress

  • Learners enter through the trail instead of navigating course by course.
  • Course-based items continue to use Moodle's own enrollment and access rules.
  • Progress can reflect the state of the underlying learning items.
  • The administrative interface lets managers build and order the larger learning journey.
  • Subplugins can add new kinds of trail items without replacing the main trail workflow.

Designed for programs and pathways

Kopere Trail is useful when one learning experience is larger than a single Moodle course: onboarding paths, certification journeys, corporate programs, curricula and other structured sequences can be represented without duplicating the courses themselves.

name: Video Annotation
description: Let learners attach notes, classifications and answers to exact moments or intervals in a video.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Annotation

Let learners attach structured notes and answers to exact moments or intervals of a video, then use those annotations as navigable evidence for review and analysis.

Main features

Point and interval annotations

Learners can mark one exact moment or a start/end interval and return directly to that location by clicking the annotation.

Classification and prompts

Annotations can be classified and can answer teacher-defined prompts instead of functioning as unstructured notes only.

Aggregate timeline

Teachers can review annotations per learner and inspect an aggregate timeline to identify the parts of the video that attracted the most annotations.

Watched-segment tracking

The activity stores actual watched segments and a resume position, giving progress data that is more meaningful than the furthest position reached.

Completion rules

Completion can depend on watched percentage and on required annotation prompts.

Learning review

Annotations remain connected to their video context, making it practical to revisit evidence, comments and answers without manually searching the timeline.

Supported sources

Protected Moodle upload Direct video/HLS URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Moodle backup and restore support.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • Resume position storage.
  • Requires Moodle 4.4 or newer.

Why this activity exists

Video Annotation mantém cada comentário ligado à evidência audiovisual que o originou. O estudante pode marcar um ponto exato ou um intervalo, classificar a anotação, responder a prompts definidos pelo professor e voltar diretamente ao trecho correspondente ao clicar na anotação.

Learning flow

1. Teacher defines the focus

Prompts and annotation categories guide what learners should observe.

2. Learner watches

Video progress is tracked while the learner analyzes the material.

3. Evidence is annotated

A note can reference one exact moment or an interval.

4. Patterns are reviewed

Teachers can inspect individual annotations and aggregate concentration along the timeline.

What learners can do

Point annotation

Attach a response to one exact second.

Interval annotation

Represent evidence that develops over a period.

Prompts

Teacher-defined prompts turn annotation into a guided task.

Classification

Annotations can be organized by purpose or analytical category.

Timeline navigation

Selecting an annotation returns playback to its referenced evidence.

Aggregate timeline

Identify the video regions that generated the most annotations across the class.

Tracking and evidence

The activity tracks actual watched segments and stores a resume position, while every annotation keeps its temporal context. Point annotations preserve one timestamp and interval annotations preserve both start and end, which means the teacher does not need to manually search the video to understand what the learner was referring to.

Teacher reports

Per learner

Review all annotations created by one student.

Prompt status

See whether required annotation prompts were completed.

Aggregate concentration

Identify timeline regions with a high density of annotations.

Watched percentage

Relate annotation behavior to real viewing progress.

Contextual review

Return directly to the exact evidence referenced by an annotation.

Completion

Combine watched percentage with required annotation prompts.

Typical uses

Video critiqueTeacher educationClinical observationMedia literacyResearch codingEvidence-based discussion

name: Video Debate
description: Run evidence-based debates where students support arguments with precise excerpts from tracked video content.
description_html:
Video Debate

Run structured debates in which arguments and replies are grounded in precise evidence selected from a video.

Evidence-based discussion

The teacher defines the debate question and available positions. Learners choose or receive a position, publish an initial argument with one or more video evidence references and then reply to classmates.

Evidence is tied to the tracked video, allowing discussion to point back to exact moments rather than relying on vague references to the content.

Video, discussion and assessment together

  • Uploaded video, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo sources.
  • Server-authoritative watched-segment tracking and resume.
  • Timeline markers for debate evidence.
  • Moodle groups and publish-before-viewing-peers workflow.
  • Weighted grading with teacher feedback and gradebook integration.
  • Completion rules, participation reports and moderation tools.
  • Moodle notifications, event logging, course reset, backup/restore and Privacy API support.
  • Transcript support and optional WebVTT captions for HTML5 video sources.

Protecting timestamp integrity

If the teacher changes the source video or its canonical duration after learner data exists, the plugin requires explicit confirmation and clears video-dependent progress, evidence and stored grades. This prevents old timestamps from silently referring to different content.

name: Video Answer
description: Collect short webcam or phone-camera video responses recorded directly in the browser.
description_html:
Video Answer

Collect short learner video responses recorded directly from a computer or phone camera inside Moodle.

A simple spoken-video response workflow

Teachers create a prompt such as explaining a concept, demonstrating a short response or presenting an idea, then choose the recording limit. Learners record with the browser camera and microphone, preview the result and submit it without leaving the activity.

Main features

  • Recording limits of 30, 60 or 120 seconds.
  • Camera and microphone capture directly in the browser.
  • Preview before submission.
  • Optional re-recording or replacement of the current response.
  • One current submission per learner.
  • Protected storage through Moodle's File API.
  • Teacher report with learner, duration, submission time and video playback.
  • Privacy API integration.

Useful for concise audiovisual evidence

Video Answer is suitable for short oral explanations, language practice, reflections, quick demonstrations and other activities where a brief recorded response is more appropriate than a text submission.

name: Confidence Level
description: Collect a four-level confidence self-assessment and compare initial and later responses for metacognitive reflection.
description_html:
Confidence Level

Capture how confident learners feel about a topic and compare their initial and later self-assessment without turning the activity into a graded test.

Four confidence levels

Learners respond using four levels ranging from not knowing to feeling they have mastered the topic. Teachers can allow a second response after instruction, making it possible to compare the first and latest state as a simple metacognitive before/after signal.

The activity does not assign a grade and does not use AI. Its purpose is to make learner confidence visible as a teaching signal.

Live classroom reporting

  • Identified or anonymous responses.
  • Optional second response for before/after comparison.
  • Real-time report refreshed every few seconds.
  • Pie, bar and area chart views.
  • Teacher control over when learners may see aggregate results.
  • Opening and closing windows.
  • Optional same-public-IP presence validation.
  • Optional geolocation validation against a teacher reference point.

Anonymous mode without losing comparison

In anonymous mode the learner id is not stored with the response. The plugin uses an activity-specific pseudonymous HMAC value so it can compare a participant's first and latest answers without exposing identity in the report.

name: Before / After
description: Capture an initial idea and a later revised idea so conceptual change can be compared side by side.
description_html:
Before / After

Capture what a learner thought before an experience and what they think afterward, making conceptual change visible side by side.

Two moments of reflection

The learner first writes the initial response in the 'Before' stage. When the teacher decides the class is ready for the second reflection, the teacher releases the 'After' stage from the report.

At that moment the initial response is frozen so it remains an authentic record of the learner's earlier understanding rather than something that can be rewritten after seeing the new material.

Teacher view

  • Configurable prompts for the two reflection stages.
  • Manual release of the second stage.
  • Automatic freezing of the initial response when the second stage opens.
  • Side-by-side comparison for each learner.
  • Participation and completion counters.
  • Backup and restore of activity data.
  • Moodle Privacy API integration.

Designed for conceptual change

The activity is useful for lessons, debates, practical experiences and other situations where the teacher wants learners to make their change in thinking explicit without framing the exercise as a conventional test.

name: Audio Answer
description: Collect short spoken answers recorded in the browser with configurable duration limits and teacher playback reports.
description_html:
Activity module Audio

Audio Answer

Create a lightweight spoken-response activity in which the teacher asks one question and each learner records a short audio answer directly in the browser.

Main features

Browser recording

Uses the MediaRecorder API and microphone access so learners can record without an external recording service.

Controlled duration

Teachers choose a 30, 60 or 120 second recording limit, and the browser automatically stops recording at the configured limit.

Preview and re-record

Learners can preview the recording before saving, and recording again replaces the current response.

Teacher playback report

Teachers get a report with one audio player for each learner response, making spoken answers quick to review.

Moodle file storage

Audio is stored through the Moodle File API rather than being sent to an external recording provider.

Automatic completion

The activity can optionally be marked complete automatically after the learner submits an audio answer.

Moodle integration

  • Capability checks and session-key validation.
  • MIME-type and upload-size validation.
  • Backup and restore support.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • English and Brazilian Portuguese language packs.
  • Requires a modern browser with MediaRecorder/getUserMedia; microphone access normally requires HTTPS except on localhost.

Why this activity exists

Audio Answer cria uma atividade propositalmente simples para respostas faladas. O professor faz uma pergunta, define um limite de gravação e o estudante grava diretamente no navegador, escuta antes de salvar e mantém uma resposta atual que pode ser substituída por uma nova gravação.

Learning flow

1. Teacher asks one question

The activity remains focused on one spoken-response prompt.

2. Learner records in the browser

Microphone capture uses the browser MediaRecorder API.

3. Learner previews the answer

The recording can be listened to before it is saved.

4. Teacher reviews the report

Each learner appears with an embedded audio player.

What learners can do

30-second response

Use a compact recording window for rapid oral checks.

60-second response

Allow a moderate explanation while keeping review manageable.

120-second response

Support longer oral reasoning without becoming a full media assignment.

Preview

Learners can listen before saving.

Re-record

A new recording replaces the current response.

Moodle storage

Audio is stored through the Moodle File API instead of an external recorder.

Tracking and evidence

The browser stops recording at the configured duration. On submission, the server validates upload size, MIME type and the declared duration before accepting the response. The activity keeps one current recording per learner, which makes the report straightforward and avoids unnecessary attempt complexity.

Teacher reports

One player per learner

Listen to responses directly from the teacher report.

Current answer

The report always represents the learner latest saved recording.

Submission status

Identify learners who have already responded.

Automatic completion

Optionally complete the activity when an audio answer exists.

Moodle-managed files

Responses remain associated with the learner and activity.

Simple oral assessment

Use spoken evidence without adding a complex grading workflow.

Typical uses

Language learningPronunciation practiceOral reflectionOne-minute explanationsFormative checksSpoken accessibility alternatives

name: Video Book
description: Build a chapter-based multimedia book in which video is the primary learning medium and progress is tracked per chapter.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Book

Build a chapter-based multimedia book where video is the primary learning medium and progress is measured independently for each chapter.

Main features

Chapter-based structure

Create ordered chapters with a title, video, explanatory text, image, files or documents, captions and complementary links.

Chapter navigation

Students navigate through a chapter sidebar and Previous/Next controls, with either free navigation or a sequential flow.

Real progress per chapter

Each chapter can require a minimum watched percentage based on unique watched segments rather than the furthest playback position.

Clear chapter states

Chapters are represented as Not started, In progress or Completed, while the activity calculates overall progress from completed chapters.

Captions and materials

Supports WebVTT captions, automatic SRT-to-WebVTT conversion, images, rich text, PDFs/files and complementary links.

Reports and completion

Teachers get a student-by-chapter progress report, and Moodle activity completion can require all chapters to be completed.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct video/HLS URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Resume from the last playback position automatically or after asking the learner.
  • Optional restriction prevents seeking into video sections not yet watched.
  • Backup and restore can include learner progress.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • Requires Moodle 4.5 or newer.

Why this activity exists

Video Book organiza conteúdo audiovisual em capítulos e trata cada capítulo como uma unidade de aprendizagem completa. Vídeo, texto, imagem, arquivos, legendas e links permanecem juntos, enquanto o progresso é calculado individualmente por capítulo e consolidado no livro inteiro.

Learning flow

1. Chapters organize the course

The teacher creates an ordered multimedia structure instead of a loose sequence of unrelated activities.

2. Learners navigate the book

A chapter sidebar plus Previous and Next controls keeps the learning path visible.

3. Each chapter tracks progress

Not started, In progress and Completed states are calculated independently.

4. Overall progress is consolidated

The activity combines completed chapters into one Video Book progress view.

What learners can do

Multimedia chapter

Combine video, rich text, image, files, captions and complementary links.

Free navigation

Allow learners to move through chapters according to their needs.

Sequential navigation

Keep later chapters behind the intended pedagogical sequence.

Chapter threshold

Require a minimum percentage of unique watched video for each chapter.

Caption support

Use WebVTT captions and convert SRT captions to WebVTT when saved.

Supporting resources

Keep PDFs, documents and external links attached to the chapter they support.

Tracking and evidence

The browser sends short contiguous playback intervals and the server merges them into unique watched content for the current chapter. Seeking alone does not increase progress. The latest position can be restored and, when seeking restriction is enabled, previously watched portions remain available while unseen portions can stay protected.

Teacher reports

Student by chapter

See progress for every learner across the complete book structure.

Chapter state
