Identify chapters that are not started, in progress or completed.

Watched percentage

Inspect unique watched-video percentage for each chapter.

Overall progress

See how completed chapters contribute to the whole activity.

Completion

Require all chapters before Moodle considers the activity complete.

Persistent progress

Learner chapter progress can be included in backup and restore data.

Typical uses

Video-first coursesMicrolearning collectionsTechnical manualsLong-form trainingRecorded classesStructured audiovisual libraries

name: Video Checkpoints
description: Insert mandatory or optional checkpoints into video playback using confirmations, answers, keywords or choices.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Checkpoints

Place mandatory or optional checkpoints inside video playback so learners must confirm, answer or make a choice at specific points before the activity is considered complete.

Main features

Flexible checkpoints

Place checkpoints by exact time or video percentage and make each one mandatory or optional.

Five response styles

A checkpoint can request a confirmation, simple answer, keyword, short answer or a choice between configured options.

Real viewing tracking

Stores unique watched segments, total playback time, watched percentage, last position and the learner's most recent access.

Seeking rules

Seeking can remain unrestricted or be limited to portions of the video the learner has already watched.

Completion rules

Completion can require every checkpoint or a configurable minimum number of completed checkpoints.

Teacher report

The report shows watched percentage, completed and pending checkpoints, last access and current activity status for each learner.

Supported sources

Moodle File API upload Direct browser-playable video URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Resume position is stored for the learner.
  • YouTube uses the IFrame Player API.
  • Vimeo uses the Player API.
  • Requires Moodle 4.4 or later.

Why this activity exists

Video Checkpoints insere interações obrigatórias ou opcionais diretamente no fluxo do vídeo. O checkpoint pode aparecer em um tempo exato ou percentual do vídeo e pedir confirmação, resposta simples, palavra-chave, resposta curta ou escolha, sem obrigar o professor a criar um quiz separado para pequenas verificações.

Learning flow

1. Checkpoints are positioned

The teacher defines where each checkpoint appears and whether it is mandatory.

2. Learner watches normally

The activity records contiguous watched segments and the latest playback position.

3. Interaction appears in context

The learner responds without leaving the video activity.

4. Progress is consolidated

The report combines viewing progress, completed checkpoints, pending checkpoints and last access.

What learners can do

Exact-time checkpoint

Place an interaction at a specific second of the video.

Percentage checkpoint

Anchor a checkpoint proportionally to total video duration.

Confirmation

Ask the learner to explicitly acknowledge a statement or task.

Simple answer

Collect one direct response without creating another activity.

Keyword

Require a focused keyword when recognition is enough.

Choice

Present configured alternatives for a quick decision.

Tracking and evidence

Video Checkpoints stores unique watched segments rather than treating movement of the playhead as viewing. It also records total playback time, watched percentage and last position. Repeated viewing remains visible through total time, while only newly watched content increases the unique percentage.

Teacher reports

Watched percentage

See how much unique video content each learner consumed.

Completed checkpoints

Identify interactions already completed.

Pending checkpoints

See which checkpoints still require a response.

Last access

Track the latest learner activity in the video.

Activity status

Combine checkpoint progress into one learner status.

Completion

Require every checkpoint or a configurable minimum number.

Typical uses

Compliance videosLong lecturesProcedural demonstrationsOrientation contentSafety trainingQuick comprehension checks

name: Video Practice
description: Provide a reference demonstration video and let learners submit or record their own practice video.
description_html:
Video Practice

Combine a reference demonstration with learner video practice, structured stages and rubric-style teacher assessment.

Watch, practice and submit

The teacher provides a reference video that demonstrates a procedure, technique or practical task. Learners watch the reference and then upload or record their own video performing the same practice.

Reference viewing is tracked by watched intervals, so progress reflects portions actually played instead of simply the furthest playback position reached.

Structured practical assessment

  • Reference video from Moodle upload, direct URL, YouTube or Vimeo.
  • Tracked reference viewing and resume.
  • Teacher-defined stages such as preparation, organization, execution and finalization.
  • Instructions and maximum score for each stage.
  • Video upload or in-browser camera/microphone recording.
  • Draft replacement before submission.
  • Fixed or unlimited attempt policies.
  • Teacher ability to return an attempt for editing.
  • Final grade calculated from stage scores and sent to the Moodle gradebook.

For demonstration-based learning

Video Practice fits practical skills where learners need to observe a model, reproduce the technique and receive structured evaluation against the stages that matter.

name: Quick Statistics
description: Calculate descriptive statistics instantly in the browser without storing the learner's entered values.
description_html:
Quick Statistics

Calculate descriptive statistics instantly inside Moodle while keeping learner-entered values entirely in the browser.

Descriptive statistics without leaving the course

Learners paste or type a sequence of numbers and immediately receive the main descriptive measures. The entered values are processed locally in the browser and are not stored in Moodle.

Available results

  • Count and sum.
  • Mean and median.
  • Mode, including multimodal datasets.
  • Minimum, maximum and range.
  • Population or sample variance.
  • Population or sample standard deviation.
  • Sorted values.

Flexible numeric input

Values can be separated by spaces, line breaks, tabs or semicolons, and comma-separated lists are also supported. Decimal values may use a point or comma, with the interface handling the ambiguity between a decimal comma and a list separator.

The activity is useful as a quick classroom calculator and as a companion to exercises where students need to inspect the underlying dataset and verify each descriptive measure.

name: Rule of Three
description: Explore simple and compound rule-of-three calculations interactively with step-by-step equations.
description_html:
Rule of Three

Explore simple and compound proportional calculations interactively and show the equation, substitution, factors and final result step by step.

Simple and compound proportion

Teachers choose the calculation mode, relationship type, initial values and decimal precision. Learners can then change values and see the related quantities recalculate immediately.

Simple mode supports direct or inverse proportion with four synchronized values. Compound mode adds two influencing quantities, each of which can use a direct or inverse relationship.

Learning-focused calculator

  • Direct and inverse simple rule of three.
  • Compound rule of three with two influencing quantities.
  • Synchronized values that recalculate while the learner experiments.
  • Step-by-step equation and substitution display.
  • Visible direct/inverse factors used in the calculation.
  • Configurable decimal precision.
  • Standard Moodle completion by activity view.
  • No learner calculation history is stored.

Useful beyond the final answer

Because the calculation process remains visible, the activity can be used to demonstrate proportional reasoning rather than acting only as a black-box calculator.

name: Mass Mail Enrol
description: Enrol existing Moodle users into a course from a pasted list of email addresses with role and result controls.
description_html:
Mass Mail Enrol

Enroll existing Moodle users into a course by pasting a list of email addresses and receive a clear result for every entry.

Bulk enrollment from a simple list

Teachers or managers paste email addresses copied from another system, spreadsheet or message. The plugin accepts common separators, removes duplicates and resolves the addresses against existing Moodle accounts before enrollment.

Enrollment uses Moodle's manual enrollment API, and the current operator can select only roles they are actually allowed to assign.

Clear processing results

  • Comma, semicolon, whitespace and line-break separators.
  • Automatic duplicate removal.
  • Enrollment through Moodle's manual enrollment API.
  • Role choices limited by the operator's assignable roles.
  • Separate results for newly enrolled, already enrolled, not found, invalid, suspended and failed entries.
  • Course-navigation access controlled by the plugin capability.
  • No plugin-specific personal-data store.

Useful for operational enrollment

Mass Mail Enrol is suited to situations where an institution already has the users in Moodle but receives enrollment lists as email addresses and needs a faster alternative to processing those users one by one.

name: Rank
description: Ask learners to rank a set of items and calculate the class average position of each item.
description_html:
Rank

Ask learners to order a small set of items and turn the class submissions into an average ranking for each option.

Ranking as the activity

Teachers define between five and ten items and a criterion such as priority, chronology, importance or process sequence. Learners reorder the items into their preferred or expected order and submit one ranking.

The interaction uses drag and drop with keyboard-friendly movement controls so the ordering task is not limited to pointer input.

Class-level result

The teacher report calculates the average position of every item across the class. This makes it possible to see both individual ordering choices and the collective tendency without manually combining each learner's ranking.

Useful for prioritization and sequencing

Rank can support prioritization exercises, ordered processes, chronology activities, consensus preparation and other tasks where the learning objective is expressed by the relative position of several alternatives.

name: Video Evidence
description: Answer questions using one or more evidence moments or intervals selected directly from a tracked video.
description_html:
Video Evidence

Require learners to answer questions with evidence selected from exact moments or intervals in a tracked video.

Evidence must point back to the video

Questions can ask for a single moment or a complete time interval. Learners select one or more pieces of evidence directly from the video and add a written justification for each selection.

Teachers can configure an expected time range with tolerance, allowing the system to score whether the selected excerpt falls in the intended part of the video while still leaving the quality of the explanation available for teacher assessment.

Video tracking and assessment

  • Moodle upload, direct URL/HLS, YouTube and Vimeo sources.
  • Real watched-segment tracking and playback resume.
  • Single-moment or interval evidence questions.
  • One or multiple evidence selections per question.
  • Written justification attached to every evidence item.
  • Optional expected ranges with tolerance for automatic selection scoring.
  • Independent weights for excerpt accuracy, justification quality and minimum evidence quantity.
  • Manual or hybrid grading with feedback and gradebook integration.
  • Completion rules for required evidence questions.
  • Per-learner report including answers, evidence, submissions, grade and watched percentage.

For evidence-based observation

Video Evidence is useful when learners should not only state an answer but demonstrate exactly where the supporting evidence appears in the audiovisual material.

name: Video Sequence
description: Teach ordered processes by asking learners to reconstruct or reorder steps after watching a tracked video.
description_html:
Video Sequence

Teach ordered processes and procedures by asking learners to reconstruct the correct sequence after watching a tracked video.

Two sequence-learning modes

Teachers define the reference steps in their correct order and can attach descriptions, accepted alternative names and video start/end times to each step.

In reorder mode, learners receive the teacher-defined steps shuffled and put them back in order. In create mode, the reference names are hidden and learners reconstruct the sequence from memory.

Video-aware interaction

  • Uploaded video, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo sources.
  • Server-side watched-progress tracking and resume.
  • Optional anti-skip behavior.
  • Minimum watched percentage before answering.
  • Step-linked timestamps.
  • Drag-and-drop ordering with keyboard-friendly move controls.
  • Accepted aliases for learner-created sequences.
  • Attempt limits and configurable feedback timing.
  • Automatic grading and Moodle completion rules.

Useful for procedures and ordered events

Video Sequence is suited to workflows, safety procedures, demonstrations, chronological events and other learning objectives where understanding the correct order is central to the task.

name: QR Code Check
description: Register attendance or participation from short-lived QR codes with session, timing and IP checks.
description_html:
QR Code Check

Record classroom participation with short-lived QR codes designed to reduce reuse and preserve attendance even when the learner still needs to sign in.

Short-lived attendance sessions

A teacher starts a projection session and displays a QR code that changes every ten seconds. Each generated code is accepted for a very short period, reducing the usefulness of screenshots or codes shared after the fact.

A valid scan is registered before authentication. If the learner still needs to log in, a one-time continuation keeps the original scan alive for a limited period so the attendance action is not lost during sign-in.

Session and attendance controls

  • Independent projection sessions for the same activity.
  • QR code rotation every 10 seconds with a maximum acceptance window of 20 seconds.
  • One-time continuation for authenticated completion after an anonymous scan.
  • Reference IP captured when the teacher starts the projection.
  • Report highlighting scans whose observed IP differs from the session reference.
  • Only the first confirmed attendance record per learner and session is retained.
  • Automatic cleanup of old pending scans.

Completion and audit trail

The activity can use successful attendance as a custom completion condition. Reports and restored course data preserve the historical attendance record, while restored sessions are closed and given new secrets so an old projected QR code cannot become valid again.

name: Pair
description: Form student pairs manually, randomly or through learner choice while preserving existing pairs and constraints.
description_html:
Pair

Form learner pairs inside a course through student choice, teacher randomization or a combination of both.

Three pairing modes

The activity can let learners choose an available classmate, let the teacher generate pairs randomly, or combine both approaches so students form some pairs themselves and the teacher allocates whoever remains.

Existing pairs are preserved when random pairing is run. If an odd number of learners remains available, one participant simply stays unpaired instead of forcing an invalid group.

Teacher controls

  • Student-choice, random or combined pairing modes.
  • Opening and closing dates.
  • Optional permission for learners to leave an existing pair.
  • Teacher report showing current pairs and unpaired learners.
  • Removal of a pair immediately makes both learners available again.

Simple partner allocation

Pair is useful for peer exercises, practice partners, review activities and other two-person work where teachers want a focused pairing workflow without manually creating Moodle groups for every pair.

name: Simple Journal
description: Provide one private editable reflection entry per learner with a simple teacher reading interface.
description_html:
Simple Journal

Give each learner one private reflection entry per activity using Moodle's standard editor and a deliberately lightweight workflow.

One private entry per learner

Each activity instance represents one journal or reflection prompt. Learners write a single private entry and may return to update it later.

The activity is intentionally simpler than an assignment: there is no grading workflow, no file submission and no peer visibility.

Teacher review

  • Moodle text editor for learner reflections.
  • One entry per learner and journal activity.
  • Private content that other learners cannot see.
  • Teacher capability for reviewing learner entries.
  • Simple learner selector for navigating reflections.
  • Backup and restore with user data.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.

For ongoing reflection

Simple Journal fits learning diaries, class reflections, personal observations and other activities where learners need a private writing space without the overhead of a full assignment.

name: Video Discussion
description: Attach threaded discussions and teacher prompts to precise timestamps in a video.
description_html:
Video Discussion

Attach threaded discussion directly to exact moments in a video so comments, replies and teacher prompts stay connected to the evidence being discussed.

Discussion on the timeline

Learners can start a discussion at the current playback position, reply to classmates and jump from any discussion back to its timestamp. Timeline markers make the relationship between conversation and video visible during playback.

Teachers can also create predefined prompts at specific moments and mark selected prompts as mandatory.

Participation controls

  • Uploaded HTML5 video, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Resume playback and watched-segment tracking.
  • Learner-created timestamped discussions.
  • Teacher-created timestamped prompts.
  • Mandatory prompts.
  • Post-before-viewing-peers mode.
  • Separate and visible Moodle groups.
  • Highlighted responses.
  • Participation grading with Moodle gradebook integration.

Teacher reporting

Reports combine comments, replies, completion of mandatory prompts, watched percentage and grade, giving teachers one view of both video engagement and discussion participation.

name: Activity Signup
description: Allocate students to internal activity groups with capacities, waiting lists and teacher management.
description_html:
Activity Signup

Allocate learners to internal activity groups with capacity limits, waiting lists and controlled self-service changes.

Choose a group while places are available

When the activity is created, the teacher can generate a chosen number of signup groups with an initial capacity. Learners select an available group, and full groups can expose a waiting list when that option is enabled.

If a confirmed participant leaves, the first learner in that group's waiting list is promoted automatically.

Group management

  • Configurable number of internal signup groups.
  • Capacity limit for each group.
  • Optional waiting lists.
  • Automatic promotion when a place becomes available.
  • Teacher control over whether learners may change or cancel their signup.
  • Custom group names and individual capacities.
  • Optional group leader.
  • Group-setting control transferred to the designated leader when one exists.

Useful for sessions and team allocation

Activity Signup can support workshop slots, project teams, presentation groups and other course activities where places are limited and learners need a clear self-enrollment workflow.

name: Request Help
description: Organize student help requests in a live queue with topics, statuses, response times and classroom resolution.
description_html:
Request Help

Create a classroom help queue so learners can request assistance without interrupting the session and teachers can work through requests in a clear order.

A queue for learner questions

Learners choose one of the configured subjects, describe the problem and submit a request. The teacher sees a central queue ordered by status and creation time instead of relying on raised hands, private messages or memory.

A teacher can claim a request, write a response, mark it as answered in class, resolve it or reopen it when more information is needed.

Main features

  • Configurable help subjects.
  • Open, Answered and Resolved statuses.
  • Automatic queue refresh.
  • Written conversation history.
  • Answered-in-class action when no typed reply is needed.
  • Teacher assignment and request claiming.
  • First-response time tracking.
  • Status and subject filters.
  • Learner view restricted to their own requests.
  • Optional learner resolve and reopen actions.

Useful during live teaching

Request Help is designed for classrooms, labs and practical sessions where several learners may need assistance at once. The queue makes waiting visible, preserves the history of support and helps teachers avoid overlooking quieter students.

name: Forum Reactions
description: Add lightweight emoji reactions to standard Moodle forum posts without modifying mod_forum.
description_html:
Forum Reactions

Add lightweight emoji reactions to Moodle Forum posts without modifying the standard forum activity.

React without interrupting the discussion

Reaction controls appear on forum posts that the current learner is allowed to see. Clicking a reaction updates the post through AJAX without requiring a full page reload.

The plugin also detects posts inserted dynamically after the initial page load, so reactions continue to work as discussions expand.

Default reactions

  • Like.
  • Love.
  • Funny.
  • Celebrate.
  • Interesting.
  • I did not understand.

Forum permissions remain authoritative

Before reading or changing reaction data, the plugin follows the visibility rules of Moodle's Forum activity. Reactions complement the existing discussion workflow rather than creating a separate conversation system.

name: Triangle Calculator
description: Solve triangle measurements interactively and display derived values, constraints and calculation steps.
description_html:
Triangle Calculator

Solve triangles from known sides and angles, redraw the geometry and show the calculations used to obtain the missing measurements.

Work from the measurements you know

Learners enter the available sides and angles. The calculator determines which geometric case applies, solves the remaining measurements directly in the browser and redraws the triangle as the values change.

Input constraints update dynamically so the interface can guide the learner according to the current triangle configuration.

Supported cases

  • SSS — three known sides.
  • SAS — two sides and the included angle.
  • ASA and AAS — two angles and a side.
  • SSA — including detection of the ambiguous case.

More than a numeric solver

The activity also presents derived geometric values and calculation steps, making it useful for exploring why a triangle solution works instead of returning only the final side and angle values.

name: Video Summary
description: Combine tracked video viewing with structured summaries, timestamp references, grading and completion rules.
description_html:
Video Summary

Turn tracked video viewing into a structured synthesis task with drafts, final submissions and references back to exact moments in the video.

Summaries connected to evidence

Learners watch a tracked video, resume from their previous position and write a summary using the structure selected by the teacher. Parts of the summary can reference precise timestamps or intervals, and those references can be clicked to return to the source moment.

The activity supports draft and final submission states so learners can refine their synthesis before submitting.

Configurable summary formats

  • Free summary.
  • Maximum-word summary.
  • Five key points.
  • Three concepts.
  • Conclusion format.
  • Chapter-based summary.
  • Minimum number of video references.
  • Word and character limits.

Tracking, grading and completion

Teachers can grade with simple criteria and send the result to the Moodle gradebook. Completion can depend on watched percentage, final submission or both, while reports show viewing progress, draft/submission state, references, grade and status.

name: Video Mission
description: Turn a video into a mission-based activity with required or optional tasks tied to moments, intervals and questions.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Mission

Transform a video into a mission-based Moodle activity in which learners complete required or optional tasks tied to moments, intervals, questions and observations.

Main features

Six mission types

Create missions for a video moment, a video interval, a question, an observation, repeated occurrences or a simple task confirmation.

Mission rules and points

Mark missions as mandatory or optional, assign points and choose whether learners may complete them in any order or sequentially.

Real viewing progress

Tracks unique watched segments, total playback time, watched percentage and the learner's last position instead of assuming that reaching the end means the whole video was watched.

Reports and grading

Teachers can review mission status, responses, selected moments, earned points and watched percentage for each learner, with grades synchronized to the Moodle gradebook.

Completion rules

Activity completion can require all mandatory missions, a minimum watched percentage, or both.

Resume and seeking control

Playback can resume from the stored position and the activity can restrict seeking into portions of the video the learner has not yet watched.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct HTTP/HTTPS video URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Backup and restore support.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • External AJAX functions.
  • English and Brazilian Portuguese language packs.
  • Mustache templates and AMD JavaScript.

Why this activity exists

Video Mission transforma o vídeo em uma atividade orientada por objetivos. Em vez de considerar o play como participação suficiente, o professor define missões que exigem que o estudante encontre evidências, selecione momentos, delimite intervalos, responda perguntas, registre observações ou confirme tarefas.

Learning flow

1. Video as the context

The video is the source material and the timeline becomes part of the activity, not merely a media player.

2. Missions define the objective

Each mission tells the learner what must be found, explained, confirmed or observed.

3. Evidence is stored

Responses can include text, exact moments, intervals and repeated occurrence timestamps.

4. Progress is consolidated

The activity combines mission status, points and real watched-video progress.

What learners can do

Moment mission

The learner identifies one exact point in the video where the requested event or evidence occurs.

Interval mission

The learner defines a start and end point when the relevant evidence spans a period.

Question mission

A textual answer can be attached to the learning objective without separating it from the video activity.

Observation mission

The learner records an interpretation or observation based on the audiovisual evidence.

Occurrence mission

The activity can require several occurrences of the same event and preserve every selected timestamp.

Confirmation mission

A lightweight confirmation can be used when the mission represents a concrete task or verification.

Tracking and evidence

The tracking model stores unique watched segments, total playback time, last position and watched percentage. Rewatching does not artificially increase the unique percentage, while the total playback time still records repeated study. Seeking can also be restricted so the learner cannot jump far beyond portions already watched.

Teacher reports

Mission status

See completed, pending and locked missions for each learner.

Answers and evidence

Review text responses, moments, intervals and repeated occurrences.

Points

See points earned per mission and the consolidated score.

Viewing progress

Compare mission completion with the percentage of unique video content actually watched.

Gradebook

Mission points can be synchronized with the Moodle gradebook.

Completion

Completion can require mandatory missions, a minimum watched percentage, or both.

Typical uses

Case-based learningTechnical demonstrationsClinical observationMedia analysisProcedural trainingEvidence-finding activities

name: Video Interview
description: Run sequential or conditional video interviews with text, uploaded media or browser-recorded responses.
description_html:
Video Interview

Build sequential or conditional interview activities with recorded prompts and text, audio or video learner responses.

Question-by-question interview flow

Teachers create an interview sequence using fixed or conditional progression. Questions can use recorded video prompts, while learners respond with text, uploaded audio or video, or in-browser recording when the browser supports MediaRecorder.

Per-question time limits help keep responses focused and make the activity suitable for interview practice, oral assessment and scenario-based questioning.

Attempts and assessment

  • Fixed or conditional question sequence.
  • Prompt video from Moodle upload, direct URL, YouTube or Vimeo.
  • Text, uploaded audio, uploaded video and browser-recorded responses.
  • Per-question response time limits.
  • One, multiple or unlimited interview attempts.
  • Optional review/edit stage before final submission.
  • Assessment criteria with score, weight and teacher feedback.
  • Moodle gradebook integration.

Progress and reporting

Teacher reports can distinguish started, answered, submitted and evaluated states and include the resulting grade. HTML5 prompt videos can also use viewing-progress and resume information.

name: Video Quiz
description: Pause a video at configured moments to ask graded questions while tracking watched segments and completion.
description_html:
Video Quiz

Pause a video at teacher-defined moments, collect answers and combine question performance with real viewing progress.

Questions appear on the timeline

Teachers place questions at specific video positions. Playback pauses automatically at each configured point, the learner answers and receives the configured feedback before continuing according to the activity rules.

Question and video options

  • Multiple choice, true/false, short answer and multiple-answer questions.
  • Mandatory or optional questions.
  • One or multiple attempts per question.
  • Correct and incorrect feedback.
  • Configurable points and optional later answer changes.
  • Uploaded video, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • WebVTT captions and poster image for HTML5 sources.
  • Watched-segment tracking and resume playback.

Flexible grading and completion

Grades can be based on questions only, watched percentage only or a configurable combination of both. Moodle completion can require a minimum watched percentage, all mandatory questions, a minimum grade or a combination of those conditions.

name: BookFlow
description: Interactive book activity with chapters, rich content blocks, reading progress, completion rules, bookmarks, notes, search, reports, import/export, and backup/restore support.
description_html:
BookFlow

Create structured interactive books with chapters, rich content blocks, reading progress, learner notes and completion rules in a single course activity.

Build content from chapters and blocks

BookFlow supports chapters and subchapters containing independent content blocks. Available blocks include HTML, Markdown, callouts, images, video, audio, downloads, code, accordions, tabs, disclosures, flashcards and questions, allowing one reading activity to mix explanation and interaction.

Progress based on what matters

Content blocks can participate in progress with different weights, be ignored for progress, or be marked as required. Chapters can also be required, and the activity supports percentage-based, required-content, combined and required-chapter completion strategies.

Learners can resume from their last chapter and block instead of searching manually for where they stopped.

Tools for active reading

  • Private bookmarks for returning to important places.
  • Private notes attached to the reading experience.
  • Internal search across the book.
  • Flashcards and question blocks alongside regular content.

Content management and reporting

Teachers can reorder content, review student, chapter and content reports, and move material in or out through Standard Book, HTML and Markdown imports plus HTML, Markdown, ZIP and print exports. Activity and learner data can also participate in backup and restore.

name: Agreement
description: Publish a versioned agreement and record an explicit immutable Agree or Disagree decision for audit purposes.
description_html:
Agreement

Publish a policy, declaration or term that requires each participant to record an explicit Agree or Disagree decision against the exact version they received.

More than a viewed flag

Agreement creates an explicit decision record rather than treating page access as acceptance. Each learner response is immutable for that version of the agreement and remains tied to the exact text that was shown.

Changing the agreement text or text format automatically creates a new version. Learners must respond again, while earlier decisions remain preserved with the historical version.

Audit-oriented behavior

  • Explicit Agree or Disagree response.
  • Separate capabilities for responding and read-only viewing.
  • One immutable response per learner and agreement version.
  • Automatic version creation when the agreement content changes.
  • Date and time stored for each decision.
  • SHA-256 content hash for each version.
  • Teacher report for current status, version history and response history.
  • Backup/restore and Moodle Privacy API support.

Suitable for policies and declarations

The versioned model is useful when institutions need to know not only that a learner accepted something, but exactly which wording was presented at the time of the decision.

name: Video Prediction
description: Pause video at teacher-defined points and require learners to predict outcomes before playback continues.
description_html:
Video Prediction

Pause a video before important moments and require learners to predict what will happen before the real outcome is revealed.

Prediction before continuation

Teachers create prediction points on the video timeline. At a mandatory point, playback stops and the learner must save the original prediction before continuing, preserving what they thought before seeing the outcome.

A separate reveal time can define when the actual result becomes visible, and an optional reflection can ask learners whether and why their understanding changed.

Prediction formats and playback

  • Open response, multiple choice, true/false and possible-outcome questions.
  • Multiple prediction points in one video.
  • Immutable original predictions after submission.
  • Separate outcome reveal time.
  • Optional post-result reflection.
  • HTML5 upload/direct URL, HLS, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Watched-segment tracking, resume and seek protection.
  • Timeline markers for prediction points.

Assessment and reporting

Objective predictions can be scored automatically while open responses support teacher grading. Grades can use prediction score, viewing progress or a blended model, and reports show responses, correctness, reflections, viewing progress and whether understanding changed.

name: Hand Raise
description: Manage a live speaking queue where learners request a turn and teachers mark requests as attended.
description_html:
Hand Raise

Organize requests to speak during live classes and synchronous sessions with a simple first-in, first-out queue.

A queue instead of competing for attention

Learners click the request-to-speak action and enter the queue in arrival order. They can see their own position and cancel the request if they no longer need to speak.

Teachers see the named queue with request time and waiting time and remove participants as they are served.

Live updating workflow

  • First-in, first-out ordering.
  • Learner view of personal position and total queue size.
  • Learner cancellation.
  • Teacher view of participant names, request time and waiting time.
  • Served action for removing the current request.
  • Automatic AJAX refresh without reloading the page.

Privacy-aware student view

Learners do not receive the names of other queued participants through the API. Only users with the queue-management capability can access the named list, making the activity suitable for classrooms, tutoring, webinars and workshops.

name: Trigonometry
description: Provide an interactive browser-based trigonometry calculator with degree, radian and unit-circle views.
description_html:
Trigonometry

Explore sine, cosine, tangent, inverse functions and the unit circle through an interactive calculator inside Moodle.

Calculate and visualize

Learners can enter angles in degrees or radians and calculate sine, cosine and tangent. Inverse sine, cosine and tangent are also available, with results shown in both degree and radian forms where appropriate.

The activity handles the valid domains of inverse sine and cosine and presents common trigonometric identities alongside the interactive calculations.

Interactive unit circle

  • Degree and radian angle input.
  • Sine, cosine and tangent.
  • Arc sine, arc cosine and arc tangent.
  • Inverse-function results in degrees and radians.
  • Interactive unit circle with x/y projections.
  • Tangent visualization.
  • Draggable point and angle slider.
  • Common trigonometric identities and relationships.

A browser-based learning tool

All calculations run locally in the browser. The plugin does not store learner answers, making the activity suitable for guided exploration, demonstrations and practice rather than a submission workflow.

name: Fractions
description: Simplify, compare and calculate fractions while showing the arithmetic steps used for each result.
description_html:
Fractions

Simplify, compare and calculate with fractions while showing the mathematical steps behind every result.

Fraction operations in one activity

Learners can simplify fractions, compare two fractions, add, subtract, multiply and divide them, or convert between fraction and decimal forms.

The calculator runs in the browser, so entered values are not stored as learner submissions.

Show the reasoning, not only the answer

  • Greatest common divisor using the Euclidean algorithm.
  • Least common multiple for equivalent denominators.
  • Cross multiplication for comparisons.
  • Step-by-step simplification.
  • Addition and subtraction with denominator conversion.
  • Multiplication and division of fractions.
  • Fraction-to-decimal and decimal-to-fraction conversion.

Useful for guided practice

Because the activity exposes the intermediate calculations, it can support classroom explanation and self-practice without behaving like a hidden calculator that returns only a final value.

name: Video Reflection
description: Combine tracked video viewing with timed reflection prompts, learner notes, questions and class analysis.
description_html:
Video Reflection

Combine tracked video viewing with teacher prompts and learner reflections attached to precise moments on the timeline.

Reflect while watching

Teachers can create general prompts or prompts linked to a specific video time. Learners can also create their own reflections and questions while watching, keeping the reflective process connected to the exact content that triggered it.

Timed prompts and reflections are clickable, allowing the player to jump directly back to the referenced moment.

Video and reflection features

  • Uploaded file, direct media URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Real watched-segment tracking.
  • Configurable resume behavior.
  • General and timestamped teacher prompts.
  • Required prompts for completion.
  • Learner-created reflections and questions.
  • Private or shared-class mode.
  • Completion by watched percentage, reflection count and required prompts.

Reports for metacognitive review

Individual and class reports help teachers see participation and identify video moments that attract the greatest concentration of reflections or questions.

name: Video Lesson
description: Turn one video into a structured chapter-based lesson with independent progress and complementary materials.
description_html:
Video Lesson

Turn one video into a structured lesson with chapters, independent progress and complementary learning material for each stage.

Chapters with their own learning requirements

Teachers divide the video by timecode and can mark chapters as required or optional. Each chapter tracks its own viewing percentage and status, and sequential locking can require one chapter to be completed before the next becomes available.

A chapter can contain complementary text, images, PDFs, files, links, questions or activity guidance, and selected complementary items can themselves be required for chapter completion.

Tracked video lesson features

  • Uploaded video, direct URL/HLS, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • WebVTT captions for HTML5 sources.
  • Per-chapter watched percentage and status.
  • Optional sequential chapter locking.
  • Required and optional chapters.
  • Complementary resources per chapter.
  • Overall lesson progress.
  • Resume from the latest server-validated position.
  • Per-learner and per-chapter progress reporting.

Completion and gradebook

Overall completion can require all mandatory chapters or a configured progress percentage. The overall progress value can also be published to the Moodle gradebook, giving the structured lesson a measurable course-level result.

name: Video Marker
description: Ask learners to identify precise moments or intervals in a video and integrate the selections with tracking and grading.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Marker

Turn video observation into an assessable activity by asking learners to identify the exact moment or complete interval in which something happens.

Video Marker is designed for learning activities where understanding when an event occurs is part of the objective. Instead of answering only with text or multiple choice, the learner watches the video and places markers directly on its timeline.

Point and interval questions

Teachers can create different kinds of temporal questions depending on what learners need to recognise in the video.

  • Point questions: the learner marks one precise moment, such as when an error, action, symptom or important event first occurs.
  • Interval questions: the learner marks the complete beginning and end of a segment, such as the full duration of an incorrect procedure.
  • Multiple markers: a question can require more than one point or interval when the same event appears several times.

For point questions, the teacher can define a correctness window around the expected second. For interval questions, expected start and end boundaries can use configurable tolerance. This makes grading suitable for real video observation, where a small temporal difference should not necessarily make an otherwise correct answer wrong.

Automatic evaluation and feedback

The activity compares the learner's submitted markers with the expected positions configured by the teacher. It can record whether each answer is correct, how far the marker is from the expected target, the resulting grade and completion of required questions.

Retry and feedback behaviour can be configured per question, allowing the activity to be used both for formative practice and for graded observation exercises.

Video progress is part of the activity

Video Marker also tracks viewing progress. The learner can resume playback from where they stopped, while the activity records watched percentage together with the marker answers. This allows completion rules to consider both the required questions and actual engagement with the video.

Supported video sources

  • Protected Moodle video upload.
  • Direct video URL.
  • YouTube.
  • Vimeo.

Teacher review

Teachers can review attempts with the learner's markers, marker accuracy, grades, watched percentage and completion status. This provides more useful evidence than a simple correct/incorrect result and helps identify whether a learner recognised the right event but selected it slightly too early or too late.

Useful for observation-based learning

Video Marker is especially useful when learners need to recognise events in sequence or detect evidence inside audiovisual material, including procedural training, safety analysis, sports technique, clinical observation, teacher education, language analysis and media studies.

name: Probability Simulator
description: Simulate coins, dice and configurable urn outcomes and compare observed frequencies with theoretical probability.
description_html:
Probability Simulator

Compare theoretical probability with observed frequency by running repeated simulations directly in the browser.

Run the same experiment many times

Learners choose an experiment and run 10, 100 or 1,000 trials. The activity compares the simulated distribution with the theoretical probability so learners can see how observed frequency behaves as the number of repetitions grows.

Simulation results are calculated in the browser and individual runs are not stored.

Included experiments

  • Coin with a configurable probability of heads.
  • Die with between 2 and 100 sides.
  • Urn with any number of named outcomes and configurable quantities.

Useful for probability intuition

The activity supports demonstrations and practice around expected probability, random variation and the relationship between small samples and larger numbers of trials.

name: Subcourse
description: Use the final grade from another Moodle course as the grade of an activity in the current course.
description_html:
Subcourse

Use the final grade from another Moodle course as the grade for an activity in the current course.

Connect course structures through grades

Subcourse behaves like a graded activity inside the main course, but its learner grade is taken from the final grade of a referenced course.

This allows course designers to split a larger learning program into separate Moodle courses while still representing the result of each referenced course inside the main course.

Typical workflow

  • Create a main course and one or more courses that act as subcourses.
  • Add a Subcourse activity in the main course for each referenced course.
  • Enroll learners in both the main course and the referenced courses.
  • Let learners complete the referenced course normally.
  • Use the referenced course final grade as the grade shown by the Subcourse activity.

Useful for modular course design

Subcourse is useful when a curriculum is intentionally divided into reusable course units but the parent course still needs one activity-level result representing each unit.

name: Traffic Light
description: Collect a quick green, yellow or red understanding signal from learners during class.
description_html:
Traffic Light

Give learners a fast way to tell the teacher whether they understand, are unsure or need help.

A current-state classroom signal

Learners choose one of three states: green when they understand and are following well, yellow when they have doubts or need review, and red when they need help or do not understand.

Each learner keeps only one current response. If the learner changes state, the previous value is replaced so the dashboard reflects the present situation rather than building a response history.

Teacher dashboard

  • Current totals for green, yellow and red.
  • Percentages for each state.
  • Learners grouped by their selected status.
  • A view of who has not responded yet.
  • Immediate class-level feedback without requiring a graded quiz or long form.

Useful during live teaching

Traffic Light can be used while explaining a topic, after an exercise or before moving to the next part of a lesson. It gives the teacher a quick signal for deciding whether to continue, review or provide targeted help.

name: Rewards
description: Connect reusable digital rewards to activity completion and show learners issued reward experiences.
description_html:
Rewards

Connect reusable digital rewards to Moodle activity completion and give learners a place to see the reward experiences they have received.

Rewards connected to learning progress

The plugin is designed around the relationship between activity completion and reusable digital rewards. Instead of treating recognition as an isolated message, it connects rewards to learning progress already recorded by Moodle.

Learners can then access the reward experiences that have been issued to them as part of their course participation, keeping recognition visible after the original learning action has been completed.

Reusable recognition

The same reward concept can be reused across learning activities, helping course designers create a consistent recognition experience without rebuilding the reward for every individual activity.

This makes the plugin useful when recognition is intended to be part of the learning journey rather than a one-off notification attached to a single page.

Learner-facing experience

The learner view focuses on rewards that have actually been issued, providing a simple place to revisit recognition associated with completed learning actions.

name: Video Peer Review
description: Collect timestamped video feedback and criterion-based teacher or peer assessment.
description_html:
Video Peer Review

Collect timestamped feedback and criterion-based assessment on a common video or on videos submitted by learners.

Two review models

Teachers can publish one common video for the class to evaluate or allow every learner to submit a video that will be reviewed by the teacher and/or assigned peers.

Comments are timestamped, so reviewers can point to an exact moment and later jump directly back to that part of the video.

Peer-review workflow

  • Common-video and learner-submission modes.
  • Uploaded video, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Timestamped comments with click-to-seek navigation.
  • Numeric and concept-based criteria.
  • Optional feedback for each criterion.
  • Automatic peer allocation with configurable reviews per learner.
  • Anonymous peer display for learners while teachers retain audit visibility.
  • Optional delayed release of received reviews.

Progress, grades and reports

The activity records viewing progress per evaluator and reviewed video. Reports cover reviews received, reviews performed, progress and grades, while learner-submission mode can publish grades to the Moodle gradebook and use completion rules for submission and assigned reviews.

name: Quick Decision
description: Run fast single-choice decisions where there is no correct answer and results visibility is configurable.
description_html:
Quick Decision

Run a fast single-choice decision where there is no correct answer and the goal is preference, prioritization or consensus.

One question, several alternatives

The teacher creates one question with two or more options. Each learner keeps one current response and can change it while the activity is open when the teacher allows changes.

Typical uses include choosing the next topic, selecting a meeting time, prioritizing projects or checking the group's preferred direction.

Control when results appear

  • Results can remain hidden.
  • Results can appear after the learner votes.
  • Results can remain visible throughout the activity.
  • Results can become visible only after the activity closes.
  • Learners can be allowed or prevented from changing their choice.

Designed for decisions, not assessment

Quick Decision does not assume one answer is correct. It provides a compact decision workflow for situations where the class needs to choose, prioritize or reveal preferences.

name: Class Pulse
description: Collect a quick classroom understanding signal and display aggregated live charts to the teacher.
description_html:
Class Pulse

Collect a fast signal of learner understanding and watch the class distribution update while a lesson is in progress.

Four levels of understanding

The default options range from not understanding through partial understanding to understanding and mastery. Teachers can use the activity as a low-friction check during or after an explanation.

Learners may be allowed or prevented from changing their response, depending on whether the teacher wants a fixed snapshot or a continuously updated pulse.

Live aggregate report

  • Automatic report refresh while the dashboard is open.
  • Pie, bar and line chart views.
  • Anonymous or identified mode.
  • Teacher-configurable question.
  • Teacher-configurable response-change policy.

Anonymous mode with duplicate protection

When anonymous mode is enabled, the learner id is stored as zero. The activity uses an activity-specific HMAC SHA-256 value only to prevent duplicate responses, while the teacher dashboard receives aggregate counts rather than that identifier.

name: Ohm's Law
description: Calculate voltage, current, resistance and power from any two positive known quantities and show the steps.
description_html:
Ohm's Law

Calculate voltage, current, resistance and power from any two known positive quantities and show the relationships used to obtain the result.

Enter any two known values

Learners provide any two positive values among voltage, current, resistance and power. The calculator immediately derives the remaining two quantities directly in the browser.

Alongside the final values, the activity shows the calculation steps and the equivalent relationships used between V, I, R and P.

Additional electrical relationships

  • Voltage, current, resistance and power calculation.
  • Automatic derivation from any valid pair of known quantities.
  • Visible calculation steps.
  • Equivalent V/I/R/P relationships.
  • Conductance.
  • Common electrical unit conversions.

Practice without stored answers

Learner-entered values are not stored. The activity can therefore be used as a guided classroom calculator and as a visual aid for exploring how the core electrical quantities relate to one another.

name: Video Diagnostic
description: Capture a pre-study diagnosis from video, release explanations and compare the learner's initial and later responses.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Diagnostic

Capture what learners understand before studying a video-based situation, release an explanation or study stage, and compare the initial diagnosis with a post-study response.

Main features

Before-and-after diagnosis

Collect an initial response before the explanation is shown and optionally ask the same diagnostic questions again after the study stage.

Multiple question formats

Use open responses, choices, video moments and video intervals so the diagnostic can measure both conceptual answers and evidence tied to the timeline.

Explanation stage

Provide an optional explanatory video, solution, teacher comments and complementary materials between the initial and final responses.

Automatic comparison

The activity compares initial and final answers so teachers can see how the learner's diagnosis changed after studying the explanation.

Optional diagnostic scoring

Expected answers, expected choices and expected video ranges can be used for automatic scoring; when no automatic criterion exists, the activity remains diagnostic-only.

Class and learner reports

Reports include selected timecodes, answer evolution, watched progress and CSV export.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct video URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Server-side watched-segment tracking with unique watched percentage.
  • Large playback discontinuities are not counted as watched content.
  • Custom completion can require the initial submission and/or a watched percentage.
  • Backup and restore support, including user data when requested.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • Diagnostic scores remain inside the activity and do not create a Moodle gradebook item.

Why this activity exists

Video Diagnostic foi pensado para diagnóstico de conhecimento prévio e mudança conceitual. O estudante responde antes da explicação, recebe a etapa de estudo e, quando habilitado, responde novamente às mesmas questões, permitindo comparar o raciocínio inicial com o que mudou depois do contato com o conteúdo.

Learning flow

1. Initial diagnostic

The learner watches the initial situation and answers before the explanatory material is released.

2. Baseline is preserved

The first response remains stored as the original diagnostic evidence.

3. Study stage is released

The activity can show an explanatory video, solution, teacher comments and complementary material.

4. Post-study comparison

A second response can be collected and compared directly with the initial one.

What learners can do

Open response

Capture the learner diagnosis or explanation in their own words.

Choice question

Use structured alternatives when the diagnostic requires a specific decision.

Video moment

Ask the learner to select the exact instant that supports the diagnosis.

Video interval

Capture evidence that spans a start and end point in the timeline.

Expected answers

Automatic criteria can be configured for text, options or expected video ranges when appropriate.

Diagnostic-only mode

When no automatic criterion exists, the activity remains diagnostic instead of manufacturing a grade.

Tracking and evidence

The activity periodically submits the real playback position and small contiguous watched intervals. The server merges accepted segments and calculates unique watched time and percentage, while large discontinuities are not accepted as watched content. This prevents a simple seek-to-end action from appearing as complete viewing.

Teacher reports

Initial response

Keep the answer submitted before study as the diagnostic baseline.

Final response

Show the post-study answer when the second response is enabled.

Answer evolution

Compare both responses side by side to make conceptual change visible.

Timecode evidence

Moment and interval selections remain attached to the learner response.

Class overview

Identify recurring misconceptions and patterns across learners.

CSV export

Export structured diagnostic data for further analysis.

Typical uses

Prior-knowledge assessmentMisconception analysisClinical reasoningCase diagnosisConceptual changeFormative assessment

name: Video Playlist
description: Place multiple trackable videos in one activity with per-video progress, sequential unlocking and overall completion.
description_html:
Video Playlist

Combine multiple trackable videos in one Moodle activity and calculate progress across the entire playlist.

Multiple videos, one learning activity

Teachers build a playlist of videos while the plugin tracks each video independently. Learners can resume individual videos from their saved positions and see progress across the full collection.

Sequential unlocking can require a minimum watched percentage in one video before the next video becomes available.

Tracking and progression

  • Multiple videos per activity.
  • Moodle upload, direct URL/HLS, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Per-video watched-segment tracking.
  • Per-video resume position and percentage.
  • Optional sequential unlocking.
  • Overall progress calculated as the arithmetic mean of enabled videos.
  • Custom completion rule based on overall percentage.
  • Gradebook integration using overall percentage.

Teacher management and reports

The plugin includes a management interface for the playlist and a report showing progress per learner and per video, making it suitable for video series, microlearning collections and structured viewing sequences.

name: Mood Tracker
description: Collect a quick learner mood check-in and show teachers an aggregated class dashboard.
description_html:
Mood Tracker

Run a quick class mood check-in and give teachers an aggregate view of how learners are feeling.

One current mood per learner

Learners select one mood from the available options. Teachers can decide whether the learner may change that response after submitting it.

The activity stores the learner's current mood response for each activity instance rather than turning the interaction into a long survey.

Aggregate teacher dashboard

Authorized teachers view an aggregated class dashboard instead of having to inspect responses one by one. Access to that report is controlled by Moodle capabilities.

Useful for quick check-ins

Mood Tracker can support opening check-ins, end-of-class reflections or other moments where a teacher wants a simple emotional snapshot with very little learner effort.

name: One-minute Paper
description: Collect a concise one-minute-paper response with optional dates, IP/geolocation restrictions and CSV reporting.
description_html:
One-minute Paper

Use the classic one-minute paper technique to collect a short learner reflection with optional time and presence controls.

A focused reflection prompt

Teachers define a short prompt, response limit and optional opening and closing dates. Each participant keeps one editable response while the activity is open.

The technique works well for questions such as the main concept learned, the most important takeaway or the point that remains unclear.

Teacher review and export

  • One response per learner.
  • Editable response while the activity remains open.
  • Group-aware teacher report.
  • CSV export.
  • Configurable response limit.
  • Optional opening and closing dates.

Optional presence validation

Responses can optionally be restricted to the same detected public IP as the teacher or to a geographic radius around a teacher reference point, supporting classroom use when a simple presence signal is desirable.

name: Matrix Calculator
description: Work with matrix addition, multiplication, determinant, transpose and inverse while showing calculation steps.
description_html:
Matrix Calculator

Work with matrices directly inside Moodle and show the calculation process instead of returning only a final matrix.

Interactive matrix operations

Learners define the dimensions of matrices A and B, enter their values and choose one of the operations enabled by the teacher. The activity performs the calculation in the browser and presents step-by-step details for the result.

Available operations

  • Matrix addition.
  • Matrix multiplication.
  • Determinant using Gaussian elimination.
  • Transpose of matrix A or B.
  • Inverse using Gauss-Jordan elimination.
  • Support for row and column vectors when the selected operation permits them.
  • Teacher-controlled operation list.
  • Configurable maximum dimension from 2 to 8.

No stored calculation history

Values entered by learners are processed locally in the browser and are not stored by the plugin, making the activity suitable for demonstrations and guided practice.

name: Percentage Calculator
description: Calculate and visualize percentages, variation, increases, discounts, margin, markup and profit.
description_html:
Percentage Calculator

Calculate and visualize percentages so learners can see both the numeric result and its proportional meaning.

Several percentage problems in one activity

  • Percentage of a value.
  • Percentage represented by a part of a total.
  • Percentage change between initial and final values.
  • Percentage increase.
  • Percentage discount.
  • Margin, markup and profit.

Visual representations

Results can be shown as a proportional bar, donut chart, 10 × 10 percentage grid or before/after comparison. The activity can also choose a suitable visualization automatically according to the calculation type.

Teacher-controlled learning aid

Teachers choose which calculations are available, define the default visualization, set decimal precision and decide whether the formula and explanatory text appear with the answer. This makes the activity useful for mathematics, finance and business contexts where understanding the relationship matters as much as the result.

name: Video Notes
description: Combine tracked video playback with private timestamped learner notes, categories, search and exports.
description_html:
Video Notes

Let learners create private notes tied to exact video timestamps and return to those moments instantly.

Notes connected to playback

Learners write notes while watching and each note keeps the current video position. Clicking a note seeks the player back to that exact moment, turning the note list into a personal index of the video.

Notes are private by default, while individual notes can optionally be shared with teachers.

Note and video features

  • Moodle upload, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Watched progress based on segments actually played.
  • Resume from the latest playback position.
  • Important, Question, Review and Example note categories.
  • Timestamped click-to-seek notes.
  • Search across the learner's own notes.
  • Print, CSV export and text export.
  • Optional per-note sharing with teachers.

Completion and teacher visibility

Completion can require a minimum number of notes, a minimum watched percentage or both. Teacher reports include only notes the learner explicitly chose to share.

name: Chat
description: Provide real-time text discussions inside a Moodle course.
description_html:
Chat

Provide a synchronous text-based discussion space inside a Moodle course for live class conversation and group interaction.

Real-time course discussion

The Chat activity gives course participants a shared text space for synchronous communication. It can support virtual class discussions, live question sessions, group work and other situations where participants need to exchange messages at the same time.

Because the activity lives inside the Moodle course, access follows the course context rather than requiring a separate messaging service.

Simple synchronous interaction

Learners enter the activity during the planned session and participate in a text conversation with the other users who have access. The activity is intended for real-time use rather than asynchronous forum-style discussion.

When to use it

Chat is useful when a course needs a lightweight, course-contained live text channel. For institutions that need a broader modern messaging stack, Moodle's Matrix integration may be a better fit, but Chat remains a straightforward activity for synchronous text sessions.

name: Video Observation
description: Perform systematic video observation using teacher-defined events, timestamps, intervals and aggregate reports.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Observation

Run systematic video observation activities in which learners identify recurring events, record exact moments or intervals, and optionally attach notes to each observation.

Main features

Teacher-defined observation sheet

Teachers create reusable event types describing what learners should identify while watching the video.

Moment and interval observations

Students can mark a single instant or an interval and optionally add a textual note to explain what they observed.

Teacher reference observations

Teachers can register expected moments or intervals and compare learner marks against the reference using a configurable tolerance.

Aggregate analysis

Reports include event frequencies, time clusters, differences between learners, average markings and matches against the teacher reference.

Final observation sheet

The activity automatically consolidates the learner's markings into a final sheet and timeline.

Viewing progress

Watched segments and the last playback position are tracked alongside the observation data.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct video URL YouTube Vimeo

How it works

  1. Create the activity and select the video source.
  2. Create the event types in the observation sheet.
  3. Optionally register teacher reference observations.
  4. Learners watch the video and mark occurrences.
  5. Use the aggregate report to compare frequencies, time clusters, learners and reference matches.

Moodle integration

  • Uploaded videos and poster images are served through Moodle File API.
  • Custom completion can use watched percentage and number of observations.
  • Requires Moodle 4.4 or later.

Why this activity exists

Video Observation transforma observação audiovisual em dados estruturados. O professor define uma ficha com tipos de evento reutilizáveis e o estudante registra cada ocorrência no momento ou intervalo correspondente, podendo adicionar uma nota e depois comparar seu resultado com padrões da turma ou uma referência do professor.

Learning flow

1. Observation sheet

The teacher defines the events learners should identify.

2. Optional teacher reference

Expected moments or intervals can be recorded as a comparison baseline.

3. Learners mark occurrences

The same event can be registered repeatedly with point or interval evidence.

4. Aggregate analysis

The report compares frequencies, time clusters, learner differences and reference matches.

What learners can do

Reusable event types

Create named categories that define what learners should observe.

Point occurrence

Mark an event at one exact moment.

Interval occurrence

Represent events that span a period.

Optional notes

Add interpretation or context to each observation.

Teacher reference

Record expected observations separately from learner data.

Tolerance window

Define how close a learner mark must be to a reference mark to count as a match.

Tracking and evidence

Watched segments and the latest playback position are stored together with observation marks. This allows the teacher to separate a learner who watched little of the video from one who watched extensively but identified different events. Every observation also preserves its exact moment or interval.

Teacher reports

Final observation sheet

Review the learner complete set of observations.

Event frequency

Count how often each event type was identified.

Time clusters

Find moments where many learners placed observations.

Learner differences

Compare quantity and distribution of marks between students.

Reference matches

Review matches, missed expected marks and extra observations.

Completion

Require a minimum number of observations and/or watched percentage.

Typical uses

Classroom observationSports analysisClinical observationBehavior codingResearch analysisProcedure review

name: Topic Choice
description: Allocate seminar, project, laboratory or presentation topics with fixed capacities and concurrency-safe selection.
description_html:
Topic Choice

Let learners choose seminar, project, laboratory or presentation topics while enforcing the capacity of each option.

Self-service selection with limited places

Teachers create the available topics and set the maximum number of learners for each one. Learners choose while places remain, and a topic automatically stops accepting new selections when its capacity is full.

Moodle's Lock API protects the final available place so two learners cannot claim it at the same time.

Teacher controls

  • Configurable topic names.
  • Individual capacity per topic.
  • Opening and closing dates.
  • Optional learner choice changes.
  • Real-time report of capacity and occupied places.
  • List of learners assigned to each topic.
  • Optional activity completion after a topic is selected.

Useful for constrained allocations

Topic Choice fits project themes, seminar subjects, lab groups and presentation slots where participants should choose for themselves but each option has a limited number of places.

name: Financial Calculator
description: Provide browser-based educational calculators for interest, present value, future value and fixed installments.
description_html:
Financial Calculator

Practice common financial-mathematics calculations inside Moodle with formulas and visible calculation steps.

Calculation modes

  • Simple interest.
  • Compound interest.
  • Present value.
  • Future value.
  • Fixed installments using the Price system.

A guided calculator

Teachers choose which calculation types are available for the activity. Learners enter the values directly in the browser and receive the result together with the formula and calculation steps.

Results are formatted according to the page language so the calculator can be used naturally in different course contexts.

No stored learner calculations

Calculations run in the browser and are not stored as learner history. The activity is intended as a teaching and practice aid rather than as a submission or assessment record.

name: Video Error Hunt
description: Ask learners to identify expected errors inside a video, explain what they observed and receive configurable scoring.
description_html:
Video Error Hunt

Ask learners to identify errors inside a video by marking the exact moment and explaining what they observed.

Expected errors defined by the teacher

Teachers configure expected errors as time ranges and assign points to each one. While watching, learners use the error-mark action and explain the issue they identified.

The activity records the current timestamp, checks whether it falls inside an expected range and prevents the same expected error from receiving duplicate credit.

Scoring and playback controls

  • Moodle upload, direct URL, YouTube and Vimeo.
  • Real watched-segment tracking, watch time and resume position.
  • Optional seek restriction to watched regions.
  • Expected error ranges with descriptions, order and individual points.
  • Configurable maximum number of learner marks.
  • Optional penalty for incorrect marks.
  • Immediate feedback or feedback only after final submission.
  • Clickable learner timeline with watched segments and error marks.

Teacher reporting

Reports combine watched percentage, found and missed errors, incorrect marks, score, grade and submission status. Class-level information can also reveal which expected errors were hardest for learners to detect.

name: My Status
description: Let each learner maintain one current classroom status while the teacher sees a live grouped dashboard.
description_html:
My Status

Let each learner show their current working state so teachers can monitor a practical class at a glance.

One current state per learner

Teachers define the statuses that make sense for the activity, such as not started, working, need help and finished. Learners select the state that best reflects where they are right now.

Changing the selection replaces the previous value instead of creating a history, keeping the dashboard focused on the current situation.

Teacher dashboard

  • Learners grouped by current status.
  • Separate view for learners who have not selected anything.
  • Automatic dashboard refresh every five seconds.
  • Fast visibility into who is progressing, blocked or requesting help.

Useful for practical sessions

My Status is suited to labs, workshops, exercises and other classes where the teacher needs a live overview of learner progress without interrupting everyone individually.

name: Completion Board
description: Let learners mark real-world tasks complete and allow teachers to validate completion from a centralized report.
description_html:
Completion Board

Track real-world tasks that do not need a file submission and optionally require teacher validation before Moodle considers them complete.

Student mark, teacher validation or both

Learners open the activity and mark the real-world task as completed. Teachers review those declarations from a centralized report and can validate the completion when the configured workflow requires it.

Moodle activity completion can be based on the learner mark, teacher validation or the combination of both.

Simple workflow

  • Teacher creates the Completion Board activity.
  • Learner marks the task as completed.
  • Teacher reviews learner declarations in one report.
  • Teacher validates completion when required.
  • Moodle completion reflects the configured validation model.

Designed for offline and practical work

Typical uses include laboratory work, in-person demonstrations, equipment setup, practical attendance checkpoints and tasks performed outside Moodle where the course needs acknowledgement and validation rather than an uploaded file.

name: Rubric Assistant
description: Create, review and safely apply Moodle rubrics and marking guides with AI-assisted analysis and explicit teacher control.
description_html:
AI-assisted grading designMoodle 4.5+

Rubric Assistant

Create or review advanced grading criteria from the assignment context while keeping every final grading-form decision in the teacher's hands.

Supported scope
Rubric and Marking guide
Design focus
Human-in-the-loop changes
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Draft from real context
Uses the assignment statement, linked competencies, learning objectives and teacher notes to prepare grading-form proposals.
✓
Compare before applying
Shows proposed additions and changes criterion by criterion so the teacher can select and edit only what should be used.
✓
Native Moodle APIs
Reads and writes advanced grading forms through Moodle controllers instead of patching core or updating grading tables directly.
Teacher remains authoritative
AI never saves a rubric by itself and never calculates student grades.
Minimal AI payload
Student submissions, identities, grades and files are not sent to the AI review.
AI Bridge integration
Provider routing, credits and model access remain centralized in local_ai_bridge.

What this plugin does

Rubric Assistant turns the assignment itself into the starting point for grading-form design. It can draft criteria, review an existing rubric or marking guide, detect overlap and vague wording, and suggest where levels or score proportions deserve attention.

Every proposal is temporary until a teacher reviews it. Existing criteria that are not selected are preserved, structural changes that may require regrading require an additional confirmation, and unsupported grading methods are never switched automatically.

Features you get

Create grading-form drafts
Build a starting rubric or marking guide from assignment goals and context.
Review existing criteria
