Look for ambiguity, duplicated intent, weak progression between levels and missing assessment coverage.
Selective application
Accept, reject or edit each proposed criterion independently.
Strict response validation
Reject malformed JSON, invalid source IDs, duplicate scores and other unsafe AI output.
Session-only drafts
Keep proposals temporary rather than creating a second persistent grading store.
Regrading awareness
Require explicit confirmation when a structural change can affect existing grading instances.

name: Course Audit
description: Audit course structure, dates, completion, assessment, content and pedagogy with deterministic rules first and AI only where semantics are needed.
description_html:
Course linterMoodle 4.5+

Course Audit

Run a practical course audit that separates objective Moodle problems from semantic or pedagogical observations instead of asking an LLM to guess everything.

Supported scope
Structure, dates, completion, assessment, content
Design focus
Deterministic checks first
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Objective errors stay objective
PHP checks Moodle data for structural, date, completion, grading, link and basic accessibility problems.
✓
AI only for semantics
Pedagogical coherence, unclear instructions and semantic repetition are analysed only after local checks are complete.
✓
No automatic fixes
The report is diagnostic; teachers decide what to change and use Moodle's normal editing screens.
Privacy by design
Learner identities, submissions, grades and private data are excluded from the AI snapshot.
Safe link handling
Authored URLs are validated locally without turning the audit into an outbound-request or SSRF mechanism.
Reusable reports
A content hash avoids repeating successful AI work when the audited course state has not changed.

What this plugin does

Course Audit works like a linter for Moodle courses. It checks empty sections, hidden items, invalid availability data, date inconsistencies, completion setup, grade-item relationships, duplicated authored content, basic accessibility issues and internal links with deterministic rules.

When semantic analysis is enabled, only the normalized course context needed for interpretation is sent through AI Bridge. AI findings are kept separate from objective errors and cannot promote a subjective model opinion into a deterministic ERROR.

Features you get

Complete or structure-only modes
Run deterministic checks alone or combine them with semantic analysis.
Section filtering
Limit the snapshot and report to the part of the course currently being reviewed.
Grouped findings
Organize findings by structure, dates, completion, assessment, content, pedagogy, accessibility and links.
Direct edit links
Take the teacher from a finding back to the Moodle item that can actually be changed.
AI failure tolerance
Keep deterministic results available even when the AI route, credits or provider fail.
Content-hash cache
Reuse only successful reports for the same course, user, mode, section and audited content.

name: GeniAI Course Builder
description: Turn a teacher prompt and source files into native Moodle activities through an extensible activity-subplugin architecture.
description_html:
AI course creationMoodle 4.5+

GeniAI Course Builder

Start with a prompt and source files, let specialized subplugins analyse what each source can become, then create real Moodle activities instead of a proprietary course format.

Supported scope
Prompt + multiple source files
Design focus
Native Moodle activities
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Specialized activity builders
Each activity subplugin decides whether it can handle the source and owns the logic for creating that Moodle activity.
✓
Teacher chooses the result
The system proposes suitable outputs, but the teacher chooses the final activity type before anything is created.
✓
Extensible architecture
New builders can be added without concentrating every content type and generation rule in the parent plugin.
Native output
Creates standard Moodle activities such as Page, Forum, Quiz, Lesson, Assignment and H5P activities.
Source-aware workflow
Uploaded material is extracted and analysed together with the teacher's instruction for that file.
Central AI integration
Generation is delegated through the configured GeniAI layer rather than duplicating provider configuration.

What this plugin does

GeniAI Course Builder is an orchestration plugin: it receives the teacher's intent and source material, extracts usable content, asks installed activity subplugins what they can build, and presents those possibilities for selection.

The important architectural choice is that Quiz, Lesson, Assignment, Forum, Page and H5P-specific rules live in their own builders. The parent coordinates the workflow instead of becoming one giant switch statement that knows every activity Moodle may ever support.

Features you get

Multiple uploads
Use several files in the same course-building request.
Per-file intent
Describe what each file should become or how it should be used.
Pluggable activity builders
Install new generators without rewriting the parent workflow.
H5P specialization
Use dedicated builders for concrete H5P content types instead of a single generic H5P path.
Teacher review
Choose which proposed activities should actually be created.
Moodle-native result
The generated course remains editable with Moodle's own activity interfaces.

name: Plain Language
description: Review teacher-authored Moodle content for clarity using local heuristics plus constrained AI suggestions that preserve HTML and Moodle placeholders.
description_html:
Clearer course contentMoodle 4.5+

Plain Language

Find sentences, instructions and content structures that may be difficult to follow, then request semantic review or a protected rewrite without handing your HTML structure to the model to redesign.

Supported scope
Teacher-authored course text
Design focus
Preserve markup and meaning
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Local heuristics first
Measures sentence length, large paragraphs, heading structure, vague link text and other objective signals without AI.
✓
Semantic review
Uses AI for ambiguity, incomplete instructions, confusing sequence, undefined terms and similar language problems.
✓
Protected rewriting
Temporarily replaces HTML and Moodle placeholders with immutable tokens before asking for a rewrite.
No automatic publishing
Suggestions are review material rather than silent edits to course content.
Markup protection
A rewrite is rejected if protected tags or placeholders are missing, duplicated or reordered.
Session-scoped cache
Repeated analysis can be reused during the current session without creating a cross-user result store.

What this plugin does

Plain Language separates mechanical readability signals from semantic judgement. PHP can count words, detect long sentences and find weak structural signals reliably; AI is reserved for cases where meaning and context matter.

Rewrite suggestions are intentionally defensive. HTML tags, links, PLUGINFILE references and Moodle/template placeholders are protected before the request, and the returned text is accepted only if those tokens come back exactly as expected.

Features you get

Content extraction
Review supported teacher-authored Moodle content without analysing learner submissions.
Deterministic metrics
Expose concrete local signals before any semantic model opinion.
Strict semantic categories
Accept only known finding categories and bounded structured output.
Safe rewrite preview
Show a suggested rewrite while preserving the original markup contract.
Bridge error handling
Keep local findings even when semantic review is unavailable.
No provider settings
Use local_ai_bridge for tenant, route, provider and credit management.

name: Role Explainer
description: Explain why Moodle granted or denied a capability by reconstructing the role and context evidence while treating has_capability() as authoritative.
description_html:
Permission diagnosticsMoodle 4.5+

Role Explainer

Stop guessing why a user can or cannot do something: inspect the actual context path, role assignments, overrides and prohibitions that Moodle used.

Supported scope
Roles, contexts and capabilities
Design focus
Explain, never modify
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Deterministic permission trace
Builds the evidence tree from assignments, context hierarchy and stored role capability rules.
✓
Official result wins
Moodle's own has_capability() result remains authoritative even when the reconstructed trace is displayed.
✓
Readable AI explanation
AI can translate the already-computed evidence into human language without being allowed to decide the permission.
No role writes
The plugin never changes assignments, role definitions or overrides.
Identity minimisation
The AI payload identifies the subject generically and excludes name, username, email and Moodle user ID.
Native admin links
Where permitted, the result links to Moodle's own review, assign and override screens.

What this plugin does

Role Explainer is aimed at one of Moodle administration's classic questions: why did this capability resolve this way here? It follows the real context path and shows explicit assignments, inherited rules, ALLOW, PREVENT, PROHIBIT and multi-role aggregation.

AI is optional presentation assistance. The model receives the deterministic evidence and the official result, and the prompt explicitly prevents it from inventing assignments or recalculating access.

Features you get

Context-path analysis
Inspect system, category, course, module, block and other relevant ancestor contexts.
Role aggregation
Show how multiple roles combine and where an absolute PROHIBIT changes the result.
Override visibility
Surface the closest effective capability rule for each applicable role.
Admin behavior
Account for site-administrator behavior and relevant accesslib gates.
AI-free fallback
Keep the complete deterministic diagnosis available without AI.
Actionable navigation
Open the native permissions screens when the operator has the corresponding capability.

name: Course Start Notifications
description: Notify active enrolled users when a Moodle course reaches its configured start date, with duplicate protection and retry handling.
description_html:
Automated course messagingMoodle 4.1+

Course Start Notifications

Send the course-start message when the configured start date actually arrives, using Moodle's Message API and a persistent delivery record so cron does not spam users.

Supported scope
Active course enrolments
Design focus
Reliable one-time delivery
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Scheduled delivery
A task checks for newly started courses every five minutes by default.
✓
Duplicate protection
Successful delivery is recorded by course, user and start date.
✓
Start-date aware
If a course is rescheduled to a new future start date, that new occurrence can generate a new notification.
Moodle Message API
Uses Moodle's normal notification infrastructure instead of maintaining a parallel mail system.
Hidden-course control
Hidden courses are ignored by default and can be enabled explicitly in settings.
Retry window
Failed sends can be retried while the course remains inside the configured look-back period.

What this plugin does

Course Start Notifications solves a small operational problem that becomes annoying at scale: a course start date exists in Moodle, but enrolled users do not automatically receive a purpose-built start notification from that date.

The plugin watches only relevant course starts, skips historical courses from before installation, targets active enrolments and records each successful send so repeated cron executions remain idempotent.

Features you get

Translated defaults
Use the recipient's language for the default subject and message.
Custom placeholders
Insert firstname, course name, start date and course URL in custom messages.
Email delivery
Force email for this notification provider while keeping popup enabled by default.
Configurable hidden courses
Choose whether hidden courses should participate.
Manual task testing
Execute the scheduled task directly from Moodle CLI when validating setup.
No duplicate spam
Use persistent delivery state rather than relying on cron timing alone.

name: Question Audit
description: Audit existing question-bank questions with conservative local checks plus evidence-bound AI review, without generating or changing questions automatically.
description_html:
Question-bank quality reviewMoodle 4.5+

Question Audit

Review one question, selected questions or an entire category and keep objective structural checks separate from semantic review.

Supported scope
Common Moodle question types
Design focus
Audit, not generation
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Question-bank actions
Adds per-question, bulk and category audit entry points to the native question bank.
✓
Deterministic checks first
Finds empty statements, duplicate answers, suspicious fractions, missing feedback and structural problems locally.
✓
Evidence-bound AI findings
Semantic findings must cite text that actually exists in the normalized question content.
No student attempts
Question attempts, learner answers and grades are not sent to AI.
No automatic changes
Suggestions remain review hypotheses and never rewrite a question by themselves.
Strict parser
Malformed JSON, unknown fields and invented evidence are rejected rather than displayed as trusted findings.

What this plugin does

Question Audit helps teachers review existing question quality instead of generating more questions. Supported types include multiple choice, true/false, short answer, numerical, essay and representable matching questions.

AI focuses on ambiguity, defensible alternative answers, wording clues, distractor quality, cognitive level, missing context and possible factual obsolescence, while PHP retains responsibility for structural facts.

Features you get

Single-question audit
Open an audit directly from an accessible question.
Bulk review
Audit selected questions without leaving the question-bank workflow.
Category audit
Review the current category while respecting question capabilities and latest versions.
Confidence visible
Keep model confidence and evidence attached to each semantic finding.
Unsupported-type handling
Report locally when a question type is not suitable for semantic auditing.
Bridge isolation
Keep provider credentials and routing outside the qbank plugin.

name: Gradebook Doctor
description: Diagnose and explain Moodle gradebook results with deterministic gradebook evidence first and AI only for read-only explanations.
description_html:
Gradebook diagnosticsMoodle 4.5+

Gradebook Doctor

Explain grades, diagnose unusual gradebook configurations and compare two students while keeping Moodle's own grade calculations authoritative.

The plugin builds a deterministic view from Moodle gradebook records and core grade classes, including aggregation status, effective weights, exclusions, overrides, locks, formulas and update state.

AI receives only a reduced representation of those facts and is used to explain the result. It does not recalculate grades, replace Moodle's final value or modify gradebook data.

Main tools
Explain this grade
Trace a grade item, category total or course total through Moodle's recorded gradebook state.
Diagnose gradebook
Flag configurations that deserve review without treating unusual settings as automatically wrong.
Compare two students
Show factual differences in values, aggregation status, exclusions, overrides, locks and weighting.
Read-only by design
Does not change grades, formulas, aggregation settings, exclusions, overrides or locks.
Core access model
Requires Gradebook Doctor access together with Moodle grader-report and grade-view capabilities.
No prompt persistence
The plugin stores no personal data, prompts or AI responses of its own.

name: AI Bridge
description: Tenant-aware AI orchestration for Moodle with purposes, logical roles, credits, route priorities, provider subplugins and usage accounting.
description_html:
AI infrastructureMoodle 4.5+

AI Bridge

Give Moodle plugins one stable AI API while centralizing provider credentials, tenant isolation, routing, quotas, credits and usage accounting.

Consumers call a provider-neutral API with a purpose and message list; the bridge resolves tenant, logical role, route priority and provider/model fallback without forcing every plugin to become its own miniature AI SDK.

Production-oriented boundaries
  • Provider integrations live in aibridge_* subplugins.
  • Provider configuration is encrypted with Moodle core encryption.
  • Custom endpoints require explicit allowlisting.
  • The parent bridge records usage metadata without persisting prompt or generated text.
Moodle para Desenvolvedores — Capítulo 32

Inteligência Artificial no Desenvolvimento Moodle

O capítulo usa a arquitetura do AI Bridge para discutir integração de IA em plugins Moodle, separação entre infraestrutura e funcionalidade, provedores, roteamento e quando vale usar as APIs de IA do core ou uma camada própria.

Ler o capítulo 32
Tenant-aware routing
Resolve tenant, purpose and logical AI role into an ordered route, allowing different institutions and user roles to use different provider/model policies.
Prioritized fallback
Routes can try providers and models in order, keeping fallback logic in one infrastructure layer instead of duplicating it across consumers.
Credits and cost accounting
Institutional credits can be managed independently from provider billing while tokens, latency, status and estimated monetary cost remain available for operational analysis.

One bridge, many Moodle features

Plugins can define purposes for their own workflows while provider selection remains centralized. This means a helpdesk assistant, course auditor, tutor or content tool can share governance and credentials without sharing business logic.

name: Personal XP
description: Add non-competitive, per-course XP and levels that emphasize each learner's own progress without leaderboards or public ranking.
description_html:
Progress without rankingMoodle 4.5+

Personal XP

Use experience points to make participation and progress visible while deliberately avoiding the leaderboard mechanics that turn progress into social status.

Supported scope
Completion, quiz, forum and course events
Design focus
Personal progression
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Event-based XP
Award XP for configured Moodle learning events with duplicate protection.
✓
Private progression
Learners see their own level, next-level progress and XP history rather than a public ranking.
✓
Teacher follow-up
Teachers can inspect participants for pedagogical follow-up without sorting the report into a competition.
Idempotent awards
A stable source hash prevents the same event from accidentally granting XP twice.
Forum farming protection
A configurable daily cap limits repetitive forum-post XP.
Grades stay separate
XP can represent effort or participation without pretending to be an academic grade.

What this plugin does

Personal XP uses gamification as a progress signal rather than a race. There is no podium, league or learner-to-learner ranking: the learner competes only with their own previous progress.

name: Case AI
description: Run adaptive case-study simulations where AI writes the narrative while deterministic Moodle state controls facts, variables, rounds and completion.
description_html:
Case AI

Run adaptive case-study simulations where learners make professional decisions and AI writes the evolving narrative while authoritative facts and state remain controlled by the activity.

AI handles the narrative, not the truth

The teacher defines the scenario, learning objectives, case facts, immutable structural facts and the variables that represent the case state. Those variables can have types, initial values and allowed ranges, giving the simulation explicit boundaries before the learner begins.

Decision-by-decision simulation

During each round, the learner makes a professional decision and the AI proposes the next narrative turn together with possible state changes. The activity validates those proposed changes against the teacher-defined schema before accepting them, rejecting unknown variables, changes to immutable facts, invalid types and out-of-range values.

State stays deterministic

The persisted case state is kept separately from generated narrative text. Attempt locking, state-version checks and unique round constraints protect the workflow from replay and double submission, so a conversational response cannot silently become the authoritative source of the case state.

Teacher review remains authoritative

Teachers can review the learner's complete decision path and enter grades manually. AI may assist with narrative and summaries, but it does not own the grade and cannot bypass the deterministic rules that govern the case.

name: Personal Progress
description: Give each learner a private dashboard of XP, streaks, goals, quests, milestones, rewards and course completion without rankings.
description_html:
Personal Progress

Bring the learner's own XP, streaks, goals, quests, milestones, rewards and course completion into one compact dashboard without leaderboards or class comparisons.

One view of personal progress

The block can show the learner's current Personal XP level and total, progress toward the next level, XP earned during the current and previous week, and an eight-week personal evolution view.

When companion plugins are installed, additional cards can show the current study streak and personal best, active and completed goals, quests in progress, earned milestones, available reward credits and overall course completion.

A dashboard, not another progress engine

Personal Progress is a presentation and aggregation layer. It does not award XP, change reward balances, complete goals or write progress back into the plugins that own those records. Each source remains responsible for its own state.

Configurable cards

Each card can be enabled, disabled and positioned in the block configuration. Cards backed by optional plugins disappear cleanly when the corresponding integration is unavailable, so the dashboard can be used with only the progress sources an institution actually needs.

Progress without competition

The learner is compared only with their own previous progress. There are no positions, percentiles, class averages or messages saying that one learner is ahead of another.

name: Personal Study Streak
description: Track each learner's own study consistency with timezone-aware streaks, milestones and optional rewards, without leaderboards.
description_html:
Personal Study Streak

Track each learner's own study consistency from meaningful course activity, with timezone-aware streaks, personal milestones and no leaderboard.

Study actions, not simple logins

The block listens to learning events such as course access, activity completion, assignment submission, quiz attempts, forum posts and resource views, then consolidates qualifying actions into one daily record per learner and course. A Moodle login by itself does not count as a study day.

Multiple qualifying actions on the same date increase the day's activity count without artificially extending the streak more than once.

Streaks that respect the learner's calendar

Day boundaries are calculated in the learner's configured timezone. Teachers can configure ignored weekdays, so a schedule that excludes weekends can carry a Friday streak into Monday without pretending Saturday and Sunday were active study days.

Protected missed days can preserve an existing streak without being counted as active days.

Personal milestones

The learner can follow the current streak, personal best, active days and upcoming milestones. Configured milestones can also connect to optional rewards such as XP, credits or badges when the corresponding integrations are available.

Consistency without competition

The block is intentionally personal: it does not rank learners, compare streaks or expose another learner's consistency. The objective is to make study continuity visible without converting routine learning activity into a class competition.

name: Personal Goals
description: Let learners create and follow private course goals with extensible goal types, progress tracking and optional XP and reward integrations.
description_html:
Personal Goals

Give each learner a private space to define study goals, follow progress toward their own targets and build self-regulation without rankings or comparisons with classmates.

Goals based on real learning activity

Learners can create goals around XP gained after the goal starts, active study days, completed activities, overall course completion, submitted quiz attempts, selected activities or accumulated study time. The available target therefore depends on measurable learning progress rather than a generic checklist.

Flexible time periods

A goal can apply to the current day, week or month, use a custom date range or have no deadline. Calendar boundaries follow the learner's configured timezone, avoiding the common problem where progress near midnight is counted on the wrong day.

Private progress and history

Learners see their current progress against the target, while goals move through active, completed, expired and cancelled states. Completed goals become part of the learner's own history, and an older goal can be used as the basis for creating a new one.

Optional progress integrations

When companion plugins are available, Personal Goals can use their public APIs for information such as Personal XP and can connect goal completion to celebration or reward experiences. These integrations remain optional and do not turn the feature into a competitive leaderboard.

name: Reward Shop
description: Provide a course reward store with spendable credits kept separate from XP, immutable ledger history and safe idempotent purchases.
description_html:
Reward Shop

Add a non-competitive reward store where learners spend course credits while their historical XP remains untouched.

Credits and XP serve different purposes

Reward Shop keeps spendable credits separate from Personal XP. XP represents accumulated learning progress and is never consumed by a purchase, while the course wallet contains the balance that can actually be spent on rewards.

Each wallet keeps the current balance together with totals earned and spent, while every movement is recorded in an immutable ledger. Corrections are represented as new refunds or adjustments instead of rewriting older transactions.

Different kinds of rewards

  • Existing Moodle badges.
  • Content entitlements.
  • Hints.
  • Teacher-approved custom requests.

Purchases designed to resist duplicates

Reward prices are taken from the server rather than trusted from the browser. Wallet updates use locking and database transactions, and each purchase carries an idempotency token so double clicks, reloads or repeated requests do not intentionally charge the same purchase twice.

Optional Personal XP conversion

Courses can define rules that grant credits when cumulative XP milestones are reached. The conversion is idempotent, so synchronizing progress repeatedly does not grant the same milestone credit again, and XP itself remains unchanged after the conversion.

name: XP Celebration
description: Queue accessible personal celebrations for level-ups, XP milestones, goals, quests, rewards and course progress without competitive comparison.
description_html:
XP Celebration

Give learners positive visual feedback when meaningful personal milestones are reached, without rankings or comparisons with other learners.

Celebrate progress that already happened

The plugin does not calculate XP itself. Instead, it reacts to progress recorded by other parts of the learning experience and queues celebrations for events such as level changes, cumulative XP milestones and important course-progress moments.

Companion plugins can also request celebrations for completed goals, streaks, quests, unlocked rewards, personal records and other supported milestone types.

A persisted celebration queue

Celebrations are stored before they are shown and are claimed one at a time when the learner returns to a related course page. This prevents a simple reload from replaying the same celebration repeatedly or silently consuming several milestones at once.

Different presentation styles

  • Modal presentation for prominent milestones.
  • Toast-style feedback for lighter events.
  • Achievement-style presentation for accomplishments.
  • Configurable visual themes and animation choices.

Designed for personal motivation

The experience respects reduced-motion preferences and keeps sound disabled by default. The focus stays on acknowledging the learner's own progress rather than turning every achievement into a comparison with the rest of the class.

name: XP Quests
description: Build personal learning quests from Moodle actions with deterministic progression, repeatable runs and optional XP and credit rewards.
description_html:
XP Quests

Build personal learning quests from real course actions, with sequential or any-order progression, repeatable runs and optional XP, credit and celebration rewards.

Compose quests from learning actions

Teachers can create quests using steps such as viewing or completing an activity, submitting a quiz attempt, passing a quiz, posting in a forum, submitting an assignment, completing a course section, reaching an XP target or receiving manual confirmation.

Quests can require steps in sequence or allow them in any order, can use availability dates and may be configured for repeated execution.

Each learner follows their own quest

Progress is private to the learner and each repeatable execution is stored separately. There is no leaderboard or class ranking, so quests are used to structure personal progression rather than to compare participants.

Completion comes from trusted course state

Automatic steps are completed by Moodle events or server-side state checks rather than by accepting a learner-supplied claim that the step is finished. Manual steps require an authorized confirmation.

Rewards without duplicate delivery

Quest completion can award XP through Personal XP and can optionally connect to Reward Shop credits and XP Celebration feedback. Separate completion and reward records make repeated events, reloads and retries safe against intentionally granting the same reward twice.

name: OabFlix
description: OAB-focused streaming-style Moodle child theme built on EadFlix, with featured content, continue watching, curated course rows, Areas of Law and live editorial content.
description_html:
OabFlix

Give OAB preparation courses a streaming-inspired front page while continuing to use native courses, categories, enrolments and completion data.

A front page built around course discovery

OabFlix presents a large featured area that can be configured manually or connected to a course. When a course is used, its title, summary, image and link become the featured content, keeping the presentation tied to material that already exists in the learning environment.

The theme also provides a continue-watching row based on the current learner's enrolments, last access and course-completion progress, helping learners return to courses they have already started.

Curated OAB content

  • Ordered highlights selected by configured course IDs.
  • OAB preparation section populated from a configured course category.
  • Areas of Law built from visible child categories under a configured root category.
  • Native course search for finding additional content.
  • Configurable OabFlix Live block with title, text, image and destination link.

Editorial choices without fake popularity

If no explicit highlight list is configured, the theme can fall back to recently modified visible courses and presents them as catalogue highlights rather than pretending that technical ordering represents audience popularity.

Focused customization on top of EadFlix

OabFlix is implemented as a child theme of EadFlix, so the OAB-specific work stays concentrated on the front-page experience while the broader course interface, accessibility tooling, login, profile, footer and activity presentation continue to come from the parent theme.

name: Roleplay
description: Run structured AI roleplay activities where learners interact with a configured character through guided turns and teacher-defined assessment criteria.
description_html:
Roleplay

Create structured AI roleplay activities where learners interact with a configured character through guided turns while the teacher defines the scenario and the competencies being practiced.

Teacher-defined scenarios

The activity is built around a character, a scenario and learning objectives configured by the teacher. This gives the interaction a defined educational context instead of presenting the learner with an unrestricted general-purpose AI conversation.

Guided turn-based interaction

Learners participate through a sequence of turns and receive contextual AI responses within the configured roleplay. The format is intended for situations where practice depends on responding to another person or role rather than simply answering a static question.

Practice tied to explicit criteria

Teacher-defined assessment criteria keep the exercise focused on the intended competencies and give the scenario a clear purpose. The character and conversation are therefore part of a structured learning activity rather than an isolated chatbot experience.

Integrated into the course

Roleplay is presented as a course activity, keeping the interaction inside the normal course context together with the activity's permissions and attempt workflow.

name: Video Bridge
description: Provide a shared video source and player layer for Moodle activities with reusable providers, capability discovery and consistent runtime adapters.
description_html:
Video infrastructureMoodle 4.4+

Video Bridge

Give Moodle video activities one shared source and player layer while keeping progress, grading, completion, quizzes, annotations and other activity rules inside each consumer plugin.

Supported sources
Upload, URL, YouTube, Vimeo, Nextcloud, Google Drive, Panda Video, OTTFlix and iframe
Design focus
Reusable providers without duplicating player code across activities
Video Bridge contains source infrastructure only. Consumer activities remain responsible for their own pedagogical behavior and Moodle completion or grading rules.
Practical results
Shared runtime
✓
One provider manager
Activities discover sources, add form fields, normalize records and obtain player configuration through one API.
✓
Capability-aware sources
Providers declare tracking, seeking, playback control and playback-rate support so consumers know what can safely be required.
✓
Consistent adapters
AMD adapters expose the same play, pause, time, duration, rate, seek and normalized event surface.
Protected Moodle upload
Use Moodle-managed files as a native protected source without forcing each activity to implement its own upload layer.
Provider-specific capability flags
Iframe-based sources can remain valid for playback even when reliable tracking or player control is unavailable.
Shared runtime libraries
HLS and Vimeo runtime dependencies are shipped by Video Bridge so consumer plugins do not depend on mod_videoprogress assets.

What this plugin does

Video Bridge centralizes the technical problem every Moodle video activity otherwise ends up solving again: where the video comes from, which player adapter should be used and which controls the provider can actually support.

Activities remain intentionally decoupled from that infrastructure. A progress activity may require tracking, a branching activity may require seeking and playback control, while a simple viewing activity may accept a provider that only supports playback.

Features you get

Multiple video sources
Protected uploads, direct HTML5/HLS URLs, YouTube, Vimeo, public Nextcloud shares, Google Drive preview, Panda Video, OTTFlix and cooperative iframe embeds.
Reusable form integration
Add source selectors and provider configuration fields to consumer activity forms through the shared manager.
Normalized player configuration
Convert each provider's stored settings into a stable runtime configuration consumed by the activity.
Capability discovery
Filter available providers by requirements such as tracking, seeking, playback control or playback-rate support.
Stable adapter API
Keep consumer JavaScript independent from the different APIs exposed by HTML5, YouTube, Vimeo and embedded providers.
Backward-compatible source prefix
Historical videoprogresssource_* provider components remain usable so existing configurations and backups do not become a second plugin family.
